items.body: Scottish artist Roddy Graham has been active for more than 30 years, releasing a substantial body of work under various monikers. Following several recent releases as Electronic Death Black Dogs, he returns with a new opus inspired by Gnostic mysticism, inviting listeners on a journey into the solitude of nature and the use of meditation to get in touch with your inner demons. He has translated this inspiration into six fully realized tracks that grab the listener by the throat from the very outset. Graham conjures a dark, sombre atmosphere, layering it with Industrial percussion. These percussive sounds evoke the golden age of 1980s Industrial music, blended with more contemporary elements of Dark-Ambient and Cinematic music. In doing so, he builds an imaginary bridge between past and present. Personally, I am particularly drawn to the vintage aspect of the work. Yet beyond the percussion, I was also overwhelmed by the monstrous sounds blasting from the speakers. Occasionally, sparse, ghostly, fragmented vocals—samples, perhaps—emerge from the darkness, and I would have liked to hear more of them, as they add an extra dimension to the compositions. Nevertheless, the work stands on its own as an incredibly solid and impressive production. There isn’t a single weak track; instead, we are presented with a succession of polished and powerful compositions. Electronic sound manipulation, field recordings, a veritable arsenal of effects, percussion, and those occasional vocal elements elevate this work to a true highlight. “The Bornless One” is an exceptionally creative and expertly crafted opus that is sure to win over many listeners. (Rating:8½). Listen to “Purification”: Purification by Electronic Death Black Dogs About Electronic Death Black Dogs Electronic Death Black Dogs is the dark ambient project of Scottish musician Roddy Graham. Discogs lists Audio Code, Blue Oma, Force Bubble, Inhuman Impulse, Inner Destruction and Nervejammer among his other recording names. The project’s first releases appeared in 2020: the album “The Hidden Paths” on Lake and the self-released “Isolated Tales”. “Dismal Dreams From The Witch House” followed on Noctivagant in 2021, alongside “A Grim Midnight Excursion” on Kalpamantra. Graham joined Winter-Light for “Hinterland” in 2023. Three further albums arrived in 2024: the self-released “The Fourteenth Step” and the Noctivagant titles “Astrotheurgy” and “Machine Spirit Alchemy”. Winter-Light released “The Bornless One” on April 17, 2026 as a limited CD and as a digital album. Graham wrote and produced its six tracks – “Leave Your World Behind”, “Purification”, “All Roads Lead In”, “Agathodaemon”, “Gnosis” and “Equanimity” – at Blacksoul Studio. Robin Storey of Rapoon mastered the album and Abby Helasdottir handled the graphic design.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以诺斯替主义神秘学为灵感，引导听众进入自然孤寂与内在恶魔对话的冥想旅程。六首曲目从开篇便以沉重氛围与工业打击乐构筑压迫感，打击乐部分明显回溯1980年代工业音乐黄金时代，同时融入当代暗黑氛围与电影配乐元素，在过去与现在之间建立声音桥梁。作品中大量运用电子声效处理、田野录音与丰富的效果器层次，偶尔浮现的幽灵般人声碎片为整体增添额外维度。所有曲目保持稳定水准，声音设计成熟且具有强烈个人辨识度，是兼具创造性与制作深度的暗黑氛围作品。

items._cn_summary: 本乐评围绕纪录片《梅雷迪斯·蒙克：跳舞的声音，歌唱的身体》展开，介绍这位美国前卫艺术家的创作生涯。蒙克拥有超过三个八度的声域，将人声视为乐器，以压倒性的音量与多变的音色模拟动物鸣叫和自然声响，摒弃传统歌词叙事。她自1970年代起便以多媒体艺术家身份活跃，融合音乐、戏剧、舞蹈与装置艺术，其创作背景与当时美国的偶发艺术和反文化运动密切相关。纪录片通过蒙克本人的讲述、作品片段以及大卫·伯恩、比约克等艺术家的访谈，呈现她从年轻时代至今在纽约简陋阁楼中持续创作的生活状态。乐评强调她面对批评与赞誉始终保持独立与坚韧，这种孤高的气质成为其艺术魅力的核心。影片记录了这位83岁艺术家跨越数十年的创作轨迹与人生片段。

items.body:
Jake Muir returns to enmossed with an album of "all goop’d up ambient bits from black and death metal records...", stirring together an atmospheric, bathhouse-ready reaction to the most extreme soundscapes, enhancing lysergic moments to bring out parallels with gear from Coil, :zoviet*france:, Pinkcourtesyphone, Main or even Ulver.

What makes music heavy, exactly? Is it simply the volume itself, or could it be the spread of culturally assured elements that make our skin prickle and our ears focus in on fight or flight terrors like animalistic cries, rattling chains or grim liturgical chants? Muir has been fascinated with Rock music since he was a kid, poring over byzantine, maximal offerings from bands like Meshuggah and Nine Inch Nails. And it's an obsession that's led him through the bullrushes of death and black metal, genres that often veer into experimental territory, crossing streams with industrial, noise and, of course, dark ambient. 'Pareidolia' is Muir's celebration of metal's nightmarish atmospheres, sounds that make the blast beats, hoarse vocals and smudgy chords sound even more substantial without technically being loud. 

Pulled away from their context, these textures are compellingly theatrical: whooshing ice winds, creaking branches, scraping metal, chiming bells, plucked strings and heaving drones. They're sounds that situate us in the scene’s ancestral Northern homeland, in some remote cabin hemmed in by harsh weather and prowling wolves. Heard on their own, it's predictable that we end up trudging similarly cinematic territory as the "dark ambient" forebears like Lustmord and Deathprod or more recent exponents Svarte Greiner and Lussuria. Muir's idea for the album was a little different; spurred on by his back-and-forth with Even Caminiti on 2022's ace 'Talisman' album, he attempted to use these bleak fantasies to power the kind of heady, sexually-charged moods that goosebump'd thru his breakout 'Bathhouse Blues' without losing the folk horror cogitation of last year's sacred meditation 'Campana Sonans'.

In fact, 'Pareidolia' is supposed to play like an illusion - even the name of the album is a reference to these phantom arrangements. Muir wants to rope us in with familiarity before waltzing us through a parallel history of isolationist, industrial ambient gear, the kind of guitar-muddling, metal-aware grot that linked Nocturnal Emissions and Z'EV and Robert Hampson's electroacoustic rock duo Main with heady set texts from Eno, Daniel Lanois, Stuart Dempster and Steve Roach. The album isn't just a collage of the quiet moments from recent RYM metal side-quests, as you'll hear as soon as you plug into opener 'Beithir'. Between the blustery soundscapes and knife-sharpening SFX, there's a melodic pulse and echoing oscillations that wouldn't sound out of place on an IASOS record, while the dense, Sunn O)))-adjacent bass drone takes on a surprisingly humid character, winding itself around weightless pads and spirit breaths.

It's the air that's heavy, not the music itself.

items._cn_summary: 杰克·缪尔从黑金属与死亡金属唱片中提取环境声响，剥离爆裂鼓点和嘶吼，将冰风、树枝断裂、金属摩擦、钟声与拨弦等织成稠密氛围。受与卡米尼蒂合作启发，他试图把金属的阴森幻想转化为带有情欲气息的温暖湿润声响，在《澡堂蓝调》的感官张力与《钟声奏鸣》的民间恐怖冥想之间取得平衡。专辑以“幻想性视错觉”为名，利用熟悉的重金属质感引导听者进入隔离主义工业氛围的历史脉络，并与伊诺、拉诺瓦等氛围传统形成呼应。开篇曲在暴风雪音景中呈现旋律脉冲与低频嗡鸣，使沉重感不再依赖音量，而来自文化联想与幽暗织体。

items.body:
Dreader than dread dub vapors from Ghost Dubs, in a lineage stretching from Dadawah to Burial Mix, Vainqueur to Resilent, Pole to Rod Modelll...​

Toiling in Berlin’s deep seam of abstract dub practice that scrolls back to Rhythm & Sound’s earliest via Pole’s dusty convections and Chain Reaction's fritzed mutations; Ghost Dubs embodies the art of dub as method with a strong haul of dematerialised, sludgy tramplers operating close to the scuzzy heart of Kevin Martin, aka The Bug. Uncompromisingly in-the-zone and dank as a bong, the dozen cuts get right under the skin, up-the-pharynx, with an intoxicatingly sedated and hallucinatory quality that impresses murky, vaporous patterns on the back of blunted eyelids and may possibly raise knees to its slompy skank and imaginary physics. 

Of course, the sound is rooted in the innovative, half century-old traditions of Jamaican dub, as established by King Tubby and Lee “Scratch” Perry, and developed by the likes of Scientist or Mad Professor. But Ghost Dubs picks it up at the point where it diffused into techno and noise during the ‘90s, taking that sound as a jump-off into his microcosm of granular, atomised atmospheric disintegration that nevertheless holds to a steady ballast of scoop-worrying sub-bass tremors. No doubt anyone who’s followed the devolution of this sound outside Jamaica, from NYC illbient to Berlin dub techno, will recognise his hands-on-desk tekkerz ushering the sound into oblique new spaces with a canny sense of proprioception that locates it somewhere in fissure between classic and contemporary soundspheres.

From the caustic attrition of ‘Chemical’, thru the inverted mulch of ‘Dub Lobotomy’, to the sensuous but elephantine trample of ‘Hot Wired’ and tumescent swell of ‘Circles Lines’ ,Ghost Dubs leaves his clammy fingerprint on every cut. Some are primed to bend your Clarks, as with the bilgy step of ‘The Regulator’, and airborne skank of ‘Thin Line’, and the harness-tugging pressure of ‘Dub Battle’, but they’re all held in check with a overarching slowness that gels the 12 tracks as a proper end-to-end listen in the manner of Pole’s early albums with a deeply reliable robustness and temper that stakes it out as arguably canonic tackle.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑将牙买加dub传统引入柏林抽象电子脉络，以极慢的节奏和厚重低频构建出泥泞、迷幻的声响空间。十二首曲目在颗粒化分解与稳定低音震动之间保持张力，既有对King Tubby、Rhythm & Sound等前辈的呼应，又通过精细的混音手法将dub推向新的领域。声音层次丰富，带有强烈的沉浸感和身体性，在经典dub techno框架内注入噪音与illbient元素，形成一种介于古典与当代之间的独特质感。整体听感连贯，适合从头至尾完整聆听，其稳健的结构和深邃的氛围使其成为该领域值得关注的作品。

items.body:
Japan’s Joe Fujinoki makes a sort of dungeon variant of dub techno, sounding something like the far fringes of the Chain Reaction label if it were excavated and screwed by Aaron Dilloway. Trust it’s completely off the rails, pulsing with life and landing somewhere between Vainqueur, Tolerance, AOKI takamasa, Rashad Becker, Pole.

There's clearly enough life left in the motions and aesthetics of Dub Techno (and its "ambient" progeny) that every so often, someone digs out the defibrillator and shocks it back to life. This time, the paddles are handled by Tokyo-based operative Joe Fujinoki, who retains dub's latent eccentricity - the kinda unsteady, obstreperous genius that runs thru everything from Lee Perry to Basic Channel - while steering the chaos into murky new territory. Inspired by "the fragility of the human body", Fujinoki extends the potential of his arsenal of analog instruments by mimicking the fluid movements of the natural world, creating a circulatory system of all-electronic sequences that feels peculiarly animate, its rhythms falling in-and-out of time like heartbeats and its tones dipping and winding like snatched breaths. 

Rather than sculpting his stack of oscillators into a familiarly fluttering nostalgia trigger, Fujinoki zeroes in on their most unstable tendencies, following a path laid out by Stefan Betke on those stone-cold-classic early Pole records, glitch milestones that emerged from the ashes of his broken Waldorf 4-Pole filter, and of course Vladislav Delay’s curving of uneven basslines and rickety clicks and pops through his loose lattice of echoes. Just peep 'Sculptural Dub I' and you'll see know what we're on about, shaping its low end into wormy spirals that inch around ping-ponging metallic smacks that wouldn't sound out of place on one of Torsten Pröfrock's most enigmatic libations.

'Limb' starts off as if it's gonna launch into a Basic Channel tribute, with distant, aching pads and a 'Lyot Rmx'-style echoed stab and quickly oozes towards total abstraction, pegging its harmonic elements to scratchy rhythmic clusters and gruff interferences. At times, 'Glass Torso' plays more like a DIY noise record, the kind of off-piste synth vs tape experiment you'd expect to find on iDEAL, or rediscovered for a timeline-distorting anthology reissue, like that stone-cold-killer Tolerance box set from a few years back. Check 'Hollow', with its blood-curdling dissonance and ghoulish pseudo-generative gurgles, or the waterlogged, freewheeling rhythms that anchor the album's euphoric closing track 'Still' and tell us it ain't special. You know what to do!

items._cn_summary: 来自东京的这位音乐人用模拟合成器与电子声源构建一组不稳定的声响系统，灵感源自人体脆弱性，节奏像心跳般时进时出，音色如呼吸般起伏蜿蜒。作品在低沉螺旋的低音与金属撞击声之间滑向抽象，谐波元素常被粗糙的节奏簇和干扰噪音侵蚀；部分曲目接近自制的噪音实验，充满不协和音与仿生成式的咕噜声，结尾曲以浸水般自由流动的节奏收束。整张专辑在电子声响的有机感与失调感之间保持张力，值得关注的是它对回声美学的偏离与重构。

items.body:
A leading light of neo-ambient takes their maiden bow on Glasgow’s stealthily expansive co:clear label after cherished turns with the sferic and Stroom labels.

The International Billionaire’s Love Child, or tiblsc for brevity, is the avatar of a Leipzig-based artist in possession of a distinctive, world-building ambient purview that has clearly stroked a nerve for listeners chasing the modern ambient zeitgeist, especially their couplet of ‘Delusive Tongue Shifts - Situation Based Compositions’ (2021) + ‘Hypertranslucent’ (2022). Those albums’ careful bends of pulpy sentiment and intricate, immersively dreamlike architecture is now echoed in ‘City of Something’, where her tender feel for compression and blends of HD and lo-fi tones fosters a gauzy sense of depth perception and sonorous emotional resonance. 

More so than her previous work, the eight tracks here are laced with a flickering pop spirit that riddles the album’s finely meshed dimensions, calling to mind aspects of Perila that are whisked to its most elegant frisson in ‘Resting Bitch Face’, or catching breathy contrails of an airspun pop song in ‘The Sun Really Is Something Round’, whilst tickling private parts of the imagination with the compressed artefacts of ‘You Just Want’, edging on Shinetiac’s take on smudged sheogaze trip hop in ‘Scare Me’, and teasing the most elusive urges on a secretive, quietly restive closer ‘Until the End of Time’.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑延续了艺术家在环境音乐中独特的世界构建，通过高保真与低保真音色的压缩混合，营造出朦胧的深度感知与情感共鸣。八首曲目带有闪烁的流行精神，在细腻的梦幻结构中融入气声流行、模糊自赏与缓拍元素，如《Resting Bitch Face》中优雅的震颤、《The Sun Really Is Something Round》中飘散的流行歌痕迹，以及《Scare Me》中涂抹感的自赏式缓拍。作品在私密情绪与抽象声响之间游走，压缩处理的人工痕迹与隐秘不安的收束曲共同构成了层次丰富的听觉体验。其声音设计兼具沉浸感与实验性，是当代环境音乐中具有个人辨识度的创作。

items.body:
Swedish jazz icon Christer Bothén returns to Black Truffle backed by Ghosted's Oren Ambarchi, Johan Berthling and Andreas Werliin, playing bass clarinet and donso n’goni over the trio's signature kraut-jazz grooves. Hypnotic, trance-inducing biz FFO Natural Information Society, Don Cherry's 'Organic Music Society', Jon Hassell, The Necks.

If you're up on your Swedish jazz, there's no way you won't have stumbled across multi-instrumentalist Bothén. He's still best known for palling around with Don Cherry when the jazz great moved to Scandinavia, even teaching him how to play the donso n'goni, a sacred "hunter's harp" from the Wassoulou region in West Africa that Bothén had picked up when he was in Mali. And he's continued to perform with various local artists and outfits, conspicuously appearing on Ghosted's 2022 debut album just mere moments before Ambarchi's Black Truffle imprint re-issued his lost Afro-fusion classic album 'Trancedance'. Last year, Bothén finally issued his first solo n'goni album and now he's back on Black Truffle with this fleshed-out collaboration with the Ghosted crew, leading Ambarchi's Leslie-cab guitar drones, Berthling's bass and Werliin's drums.

Berthling and Werliin take the lead at first on the title track, hammering out a rotating groove before Bothén lets rip on bass clarinet. And playing a side role, Ambarchi might have the most important presence, using his signature phased, organ-like tones to provide anchoring drones for Bothén's spirited improvisations. He's even more pivotal on 'Antigorite', playing cascading staccato notes over those Leslie moans and creating an rhythmelodic foil for the other three players' more traditional interplay. But it's when Bothén plays the n'ghoni that the album really hits its stride; on 'Lizardite', those buzzing tones offset Ambarchi's crystalline twangs, filling in for Werliin's imposing basslines. It's the moment where everything else just drops into place, creating a structural crescendo before the album careers into darkness on the brilliantly moody closer 'Chrysotile'.

items._cn_summary: Christer Bothén与Ghosted成员合作，将西非传统乐器donso n'goni和低音单簧管融入kraut-jazz的循环律动中。标题曲以贝斯与鼓构建旋转式节奏，Bothén在Ambarchi的Leslie箱体吉他嗡鸣之上展开即兴；Antigorite中Ambarchi的断奏音符与持续音色形成节奏旋律对位，为其他三人的互动提供独特框架。Lizardite里n'goni的蜂鸣音色与Ambarchi的清澈拨弦交织，取代了贝斯的沉重低音，使整体结构推向高潮。末曲Chrysotile转向阴暗氛围，收束有力。专辑的亮点在于传统狩猎竖琴与现代实验爵士语汇的碰撞，以及四位乐手在重复性律动中保持的即兴张力，既延续了Don Cherry式的世界爵士精神，又带有Black Truffle厂牌特有的迷幻质感。

items.body:
Our Darkness descends upon Dark Entries with a reissue of Anne Clark’s epochal proto-house masterpiece from 1984.

"As a young poet, Clark found herself drawn to London’s emerging punk scene. She became acquainted with Psychic TV affiliate David Harrow, with whom she would collaborate on 1983’s Changing Places and 1984’s Joined Up Writing. “Our Darkness,” off the latter album, was released as a single on Ink Records that same year, and became an underground club hit. It’s a singular piece of music: Clark’s lyrics, delivered with equal parts muscular confidence and unease, speak of urban alienation and heartbreak, while Harrow’s production pummels the listener with hydraulic beats and gloom-laced arpeggios. The song’s spirit would prove influential on both the early Chicago house and Detroit techno scenes, where mechanistic funk and existential despair could catalyse dancefloor mayhem.

This reissue offers three versions of “Our Darkness”: the original 12” remix, the Razormaid mix, and a previously unreleased dub version uncovered by David Harrow. Also included is the extended mix of “Sleeper in Metropolis,” another dancefloor hit of Clark’s, as well as the elegiac “Poem for a Nuclear Romance.”

“Our Darkness” channels timeless longing and contemporary dismay, a classic overdue for a little light shed upon it."
items._cn_summary: Anne Clark 1984年的作品《Our Darkness》由Dark Entries重新发行，收录原版12寸混音、Razormaid混音及David Harrow发现的未发行Dub版，并附《Sleeper in Metropolis》加长混音和《Poem for a Nuclear Romance》。Clark以诗人身份进入伦敦朋克场景，与David Harrow合作，歌词以自信而不安的语调描绘都市疏离与心碎，Harrow的节拍与琶音构建出机械感与阴郁氛围。该曲对早期芝加哥浩室和底特律电音场景产生深远影响，被视为proto-house重要作品。再版让这首兼具永恒渴望与当代沮丧的曲目重见天日。

items.body:
One of electronic music's most influential recordings, back in circulation.

Most readers of these pages will know the story, but to indulge you with a recap, Gottsching was part of electronic krautrock heroes Ash Ra Tempel and in 1981, off the back of a Klaus Schulze tour, sat down one evening and dropped a continuous piece of music which would uncannily imagine the arc of dance music for a quarter of a century.

Early adopters in the Chicago and Detroit warehouses and mediterranean pleasure palaces must have thrilled to the balanced and continuous surging flow of the hour long piece - even over two sides the mix is perfect for building a club atmosphere and suggesting avenues for mixing, whilst using merely two chords throughout. the minimalism offsets the percussive splendour perfectly - several years later the tune was rediscovered and co-opted into the huge italo house smash Sueno Latino, which cemented its foundation in the burgeoning balearic scene of the time and proceeded through several spells of rapturous revival throughout the nineties, not least when figures like Carl Craig and Basic Channel issued their own radically different reshapes and remakes of the piece.

Very satisfying then to have this Gottsching sanctioned edition, where the game might truly be said to have begun in earnest. As they say on the august walls of the Hardwax emporium - buy or die.
items._cn_summary: 曼努埃尔·戈特辛格于一九八一年录下这段约一小时的连续音乐，全曲只用两个和弦，在极简框架内形成稳定而持续涌动的节奏流。乐评认为，它既能营造俱乐部氛围，也为混音提供了开放路径，被视为提前勾勒出此后二十余年舞曲音乐走向的关键录音。作品后来被意大利浩室名曲《拉丁之梦》改编，并经由卡尔·克雷格与基础频道等人物截然不同的重塑，在九十年代多次复兴。此次由戈特辛格认可的版本重新发行，让这段历史的源头得以清晰呈现。

items.body:
An iconic album originally brought to life via Sweden's peerless iDEAL Recordings, Kali Malone’s 'The Sacrificial Code’ is a major work featuring almost two hours of concentrated, creeping organ pieces aligned to non traditional intonation/tuning systems. It's a stunning realisation of ideas borne out of academic and conceptual rigour, with a perception-altering quality that encourages exploration without a preordained endpoint.

The Sacrificial Code’ takes a more surgical approach to the methods first explored on last year’s ‘Organ Dirges 2016 - 2017’. Over the course of three parts performed on three different organs, Malone’s minimalist process captures a jarring precision of closeness, both on the level of the materiality of the sounds and on the level of composition.The recordings here involved careful close miking of the pipe organ in such a way as to eliminate environmental identifiers as far as possible - essentially removing the large hall reverb so inextricably linked to the instrument. The pieces were then further compositionally stripped of gestural adornments and spontaneous expressive impulse -  an approach that flows against the grain of the prevailing musical hegemony, where sound is so often manipulated, and composition often steeped in self indulgence. It echoes Steve Reich’s sentiment “..by voluntarily giving up the freedom to do whatever momentarily comes to mind, we are, as a result, free of all that momentarily comes to mind.”

With its slow, purified and seemingly austere qualities ‘The Sacrificial Code’ guides us through an almost trance-inducing process where we become vulnerable receptors for every slight movement, where every miniature shift in sound becomes magnified through stillness. As such, it’s a uniquely satisfying exercise in transcendence through self restraint and by this point inarguably a modern classic.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以近两小时的管风琴作品为核心，采用非传统调律体系，通过近距离拾音消除教堂混响，剥离即兴姿态与情感装饰，使声音材质与结构关系被极度放大。三首曲目分别在三台不同管风琴上录制，延续了创作者此前对极简管风琴声响的探索，但手法更为精微。缓慢、纯净、近乎禁欲的声响流动中，细微变化因静止而清晰，形成一种通过自我克制达成的沉浸式聆听体验。作品在学院派观念与声音物质性之间取得平衡，被乐评视为当代极简音乐的重要之作。

items.body:
The eminently watchable Accidental Meetings introduce extended family member, Lovely Dave, with a real guess-again mixtape (the first in a series) refracting myriad strains of blissed synths, outernational jazz, new wave pop, post punk scuzz, screwed club and dub

Six years into Accidental Meetings’ serendipitous plot, we know to expect anything and everything from the Bristol label, so long as it's got a unique soul and does not bore. Lovely Dave ideally plays true to that brief on his 99 minute mixtape, effortlessly glyding from outernational synth folk to a killer Curtis Mayfield cover via everything from thumb piano meditations, jazz-funked sidewinders, and a proto-new beat bomb on the A-side, before swerving from gothic new wave to smudged minimal wave audities, a pitch-slapped batacuda house ace, and meter-messing skronk on the backside.

Brilliantly strange but true!
items._genre: experimental / jazz / new wave / post-punk / electronic
items._cn_summary: 这张99分钟的mixtape是Accidental Meetings厂牌首张系列作品，以高度混杂的方式串联起极乐合成器、域外爵士、新浪潮流行、后朋克噪音、扭曲俱乐部节奏与配音元素。A面从域外合成民谣滑向Curtis Mayfield翻唱，穿插拇指琴冥想、爵士放克与早期新节拍炸弹；B面则转向哥特新浪潮、模糊极简波、变调巴塔克达浩室及错拍噪音。整体呈现一种难以归类的奇异感，在流畅拼接中保持独特灵魂，既实验又具备可听性，充分体现布里斯托地下厂牌的跨界精神。

items.body:
Coltrane’s invigorating ’66 spiritual free jazz salvo - the follow-up to ‘A Love Supreme’ (1965) - is unleashed from the Verve Vault, spotlighting his classic line-up tearing out on templates set by Ornette Coleman years prior, along with more reserved moments of beauty. An evergreen..

"Following the genre-redefining revelations of A Love Supreme in 1965, John Coltrane began a dramatic shift toward spiritual free jazz, abandoning familiar forms in favour of a more abstract sonic palette and bold questions he'd spend the rest of his life and career pursuing. Meditations, released by Impulse! in 1966, continues that emotional throughline while retaining, for the last time in full, the classic quartet that propelled Trane to greatness: pianist McCoy Tyner, bassist Jimmy Garrison and drummer Elvin Jones. (They're further augmented by Pharoah Sanders on tenor sax and additional drummer Rashied Ali.) Meditations pushes Coltrane’s spiritual jazz into heightened realms of energy and abstraction — a powerful document of transformation, intensity, and devotion in Coltrane’s recorded legacy."
items._cn_summary: 这张一九六六年的专辑是约翰·柯川在《至高无上的爱》之后的重要作品，也是其经典四重奏最后一次完整集结，并加入法老·桑德斯与拉希德·阿里。乐评指出，柯川在此放弃了熟悉的曲式，以更抽象的声音质感和高能即兴展开追问；音乐既延续了前作的虔诚情感，又推向更强的能量与抽象层面，同时保留了一些内敛的优美段落。整体上，它被视为柯川录音遗产中体现转变、强度与投入的有力文献。

items.excerpt: Severed Heads release an expanded reissue of their 1991 opus Cuisine (With Piscatorial) via Dark Entries. This double-LP reissue is the first time that Cuisine will appear on vinyl, with a previously unreleased early version of “Seven of Oceans.” "As originary Aussie industrial legends – although founder Tom Ellard would balk at being branded as such – Severed Heads shaped the continental subcultural sound with their kitchen electronics, chaotic tape loops, and infectious nursery-rhyme-esque mel
items.body:
Severed Heads release an expanded reissue of their 1991 opus Cuisine (With Piscatorial) via Dark Entries. This double-LP reissue is the first time that Cuisine will appear on vinyl, with a previously unreleased early version of “Seven of Oceans.”

"As originary Aussie industrial legends – although founder Tom Ellard would balk at being branded as such – Severed Heads shaped the continental subcultural sound with their kitchen electronics, chaotic tape loops, and infectious nursery-rhyme-esque melodies. Cuisine (With Piscatorial) was the long-running project’s ninth album, and is a commentary on the state of music. Ellard explains: “The whole food joke is really about what music's about and how disposable it is; people have records like they have cups of coffee.” The album also presents a turn away from the dancefloor formalism of the era, which Ellard dismissed as already sufficiently explored. Cuisine brings us punchy pop kernels of the prime Heads variety, all clocking in around three minutes. Cuts like “Pilot in Hell” and “Ugly Twenties” rank among the band’s best through their deadly skewering of synth pop tropes. But the album also offers us a Piscatorial section, where Ellard felt free to “go fishing for ideas.” Here we get a taste of the project’s demented cut-up sensibilities, like on the “Quest for Oom Pa Pa” suite, where vintage jazz records are collaged into an angular nightmare."

items.body:
First time reissue of Wolfgang Voigt's foundational first GAS album since its release in 1996 - it remains the archetype for so much contemporary ambient music and back-room techno, melting camouflaged German cultural references into a timeless, anthemic pulse. This new reissue is the original extended vinyl version, with definitive longer versions of the six classic tracks. Available in deluxe 3LP and single CD editions.

By the mid-'90s, techno had become the language of German youth culture, tied up in the country's long history of electronic musical innovation - from Kluster to Kraftwerk - and the revolutionary cry of reunification when the Berlin Wall fell in 1989. Based in Köln, Voigt had already put his stamp on dance music by the time he embarked on the mysterious GAS project, working alongside his brother Reinhard to help devise the sound that would evolve into minimal techno, but GAS felt different - more illusory, hypnotic. 

The name, aside from accurately describing the vaporous ambience that whispers through each track, stands for Germany, Austria, Switzerland, and it was Voigt's concept to not only express the feeling of dropping acid in the Königsforst, a verdant woodland only a short drive from Köln, but to distill centuries of German music into a contemporary haze that reflected a hopeful new era. And after testing the waters with '95's Profan-released EP 'Modern', Voigt set a new benchmark with 'GAS', laying out his narrative over six long movements, the shortest of which clocks in at just under 12 minutes.

Voigt wasn't interested in making songs, exactly, but emphasizing texture, burying samples of traditional German music - from baroque to schlager - in murky drones punctuated by squashed 4/4 rhythms. Not dance music exactly, it's headphone gear that's referencing the dance canon in its shift from the US, through Jamaica and the UK to Germany. Much like the Artificial Intelligence era in the UK, it imprints the familiar cycles (pulsing kick drums, undulating soundsystem-ready basslines) with its own regional character. It's no mistake that Voigt begins with an entirely beatless composition that paints the landscape without revealing the complete palette. The album's airiest track, 'GAS 1' is a stylistic milestone - something we can hear tracking thru electronic music from then until now; just listen to Jan Jelinek, Vladislav Delay, PAN's 'Mono No Aware' comp, or anything on the West Mineral imprint. It's ambient music, but where Eno's vision was trained on an earlier era, Voigt had cut his teeth on acid house, hardcore and Detroit techno, and was able to muddle those influences with his own homegrown obsessions. 

That famous, omnipresent filtered kick makes its first appearance on 'GAS 2', thudding beneath watery glitches and sweeping orchestral pads. Voigt doesn't make his concept too vivid (at least at this stage in its evolution), but the outline of classical music is there, punctured by mesmerising minimal thuds that as yet hadn't become a meme. It's not music that develops, it exists, freezing a moment in time and letting the mind pick out a scene, concentrating on the organic, shifting harmonies rather than the static beat. If acid house was all about the squelch, this was all about vapour, as sample-rich pads seem to disappear into clouds of static, blooming from the density. There's a more evident schlager-inspired swing on 'GAS 4' that Voigt and his Kompakt crew would explore more in the coming years, but it's contorted into a subterranean rumble, and on 'GAS 5', the producer tentatively glances trance's quivering euphoria, using reverb and delay to turn anthemic stabs into whooshing melodic rushes. 

If you haven't managed to hear GAS before, this is the perfect starting point, and if you've only heard the album in its truncated form (both the CD release and the 'Nah und Fern' version were incomplete), then we've got to say this is the one.
items._cn_summary: Wolfgang Voigt 的 GAS 项目首作于 1996 年发行，本次再版采用原始加长版，收录六首经典曲目的完整版本。乐评指出，这张专辑奠定了当代氛围音乐与背景 techno 的原型，将隐匿的德国文化指涉融入永恒而颂歌般的律动。Voigt 不以歌曲结构为重心，而是强调声音纹理，将德国传统音乐采样——从巴洛克到流行小调——埋入浑浊的嗡鸣与被压缩的 4/4 节奏之中。首曲完全无拍，以纯氛围铺陈景观；随后标志性的滤波底鼓在液态故障与管弦乐垫底中浮现。作品并非舞曲，而是用耳机聆听的电子音乐，在从美国经牙买加、英国到德国的舞曲脉络中注入地域性格，并呼应了英国 Artificial Intelligence 时代的美学，对后世的 Jan Jelinek、Vladislav Delay 等产生了深远影响。

items.body:
In the 15+ years that have elapsed since 'Loop Finding Jazz Records' first shuffled out of his ambrosially dusty speakers, Jan Jelinek's most famous album has acquired an almost mythical status. Originally released via Pole's defunct Scape imprint, it now finds new life via Jelinek's own Faitiche label, for a new generation to marvel at one of the finest examples of loop-based electronic music typical of the early noughties.

Taking what reads like a pretty austere set of ingredients, Jelinek's technique revolves around a trio of elements which consist of second long cuts of 1960's-70's jazz recordings, the loop-finding modulation wheel (do your homework!) and the Moiré effect; albeit rendered in the acoustic as opposed to the image and spectral domains.

If all this sounds a bit academic, be assured that on record it is anything but; as crumbling edifices of mealy rhythms slowly pulse into life and swirl around your head like snow storms clashing with a dust devil. Taking sediments of fathom deep static then skimming the best stuff from the top, Jelinek opens through the dampened echoes of 'Moiré (piano & organ)' wherein a slow-motion thrum of spiraling clicks, rustles and analogue tones conspire to give the impression of recondite perspectives that extend well beyond the constituent elements.

Elsewhere, 'Rocky in the Video Age' instills a gratuitously optimistic blush to the aquatic micro-sound ebb, 'Moiré (Strings)' is a perfect companion to Basinski's disintegrating tape archive, whilst 'Them, Their' represents an aural crease so sleight you can only catch its distinctive gleam from the corner of your eye.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以1960-70年代爵士录音的秒级切片为素材，通过循环调制与莫尔效应原理，在声学领域构建出类似视觉波纹的听觉幻象。作品在缓慢脉动的节奏中交织点击、沙沙声与模拟音调，营造出超越素材本身的深邃空间感。开篇曲以阻尼回声呈现螺旋下坠的律动，后续曲目则分别展现水下微声的乐观光泽、与磁带消解档案相呼应的弦乐纹理，以及细微到只能从余光中捕捉的听觉褶皱。整张专辑是早期千禧年循环电子音乐的典型样本，在极简素材中发展出丰富的层次与动态。

items.body:
Finally, Kompakt issue a true GAS outlier on vinyl for the first time, recorded in 1989 and containing some of Wolfgang Voigt’s earliest and starkest recycling of magisterial Wagner loops, closest to the ends of The Caretaker, Philip Jeck, Kevin Drumm.

One of those releases that has lurked on our shelves since 2008 as a book and CD, ‘November 89’ exists in the margins of Wolfgang Voigt’s GAS canon as its creepiest and most occluded evocation of long walks in the Bavarian forests. While other GAS classics ooze a sort of dappled warmth breaking thru the trees in their widescreen dub techno strolls, you can fully feel the light dying over the horizon and the forest drawing in on this particularly gloomy, hour-long suite. 

As the title suggests, it was mostly, remarkably, made in ’89, back when Voigt was finding his feet between techno, house and indie-pop, and nearly a decade before he co-founded Kompakt with Michael Mayer & Jürgen Paape - by which time he was a full-fledged rave dynamo as Love Inc. and myriad others notable projects. And, in that sense, it can be heard as his ‘Selected Ambient Works 89-95’ - or perhaps more pertinently with SAW II vibes - in his nascent attempt to chase the ambient dragon, which surely endures for its strangely nostalgic, unheimlich qualities.

An educated guess leads us to think the first three were made in ’89, taking in the nightfall scenery of smudged symphonic strings and icy crackle to ‘Der Wald’, plus the muddied bass waltz and spectral pall of ‘Das Moor’, thru the self-evidently titled centrepiece ‘1989-11-01’, bristling with a digitally iridescent dread. ‘Tal 90’ and ‘Nah Und Fern’, which shares its title with the 2008 boxset, were most likely made a little later, and find the wintry doom thawing to the GAS-eous forms we’ve all come to deeply know and adore. 

A true evergreen for deep ambient techno connoisseurs, no less
items._genre: ambient techno / dark ambient / experimental / drone
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑收录了Wolfgang Voigt于1989年录制的早期GAS作品，首次以黑胶形式发行。内容以对瓦格纳管弦乐循环的阴暗化采样为核心，将庄严的弦乐片段处理成模糊、冰冷且带有裂纹的声响，营造出类似The Caretaker、Philip Jeck式的衰败与怀旧感。与GAS后期作品中通透的森林光影不同，这里更多是暮色降临、森林逼近的压抑氛围，整张一小时组曲充满幽闭与不安。前三首更接近原始实验，后两首则逐渐解冻为GAS标志性的气态techno形态，呈现出一条从暗黑环境到氛围techno的演进线索。作品在电子音乐与古典素材之间建立了独特的声音景观，其诡异的怀旧气质和深邃的层次感使其成为氛围techno领域的重要遗珠。

items.body:
On Kirk Barley’s definitive solo gem, alternative tunings and a tactile feel for pitching rhythms generate their gentlest and most absorbing work, twinkling amid a microcosm of similar, exploratory productions from Mark Fell & Rian Treanor thru to Aleksi Perälä, Beatrice Dillon, Terry Riley & Jon Hassell.

Building on a decade of work spanning cuts for Brownswood thru to jams with Matthew Herbert and Matt Davies, ‘Arc’ finds Yorkshire-bred artist Barley fully indulge formative passions for microtonal just intonation - as seeded in Terry Riley’s ‘Shri Camel’ - and slippery syncopation to the fullest. Half solo, proper, and half peppered with percussion by regular spar, Matt Davies, it follows his nose for open frontiers of alternative tunings and wonky meter with the blend of low key modesty and prism-pushing tekkerz that have long endeared his work to lovers of lower case experimental music. 

Sweetly balanced between timeless, folk-soul-wise and futurist sensibilities, the half hour suite knits hyaline synths and rippling gamelan metallophonics with clarinet and guitar in lissom, sloshing shapes that effortlessly seduce, rather than demand, the listener’s attention. In particular we are drawn to the bits in duo with Davies, floating sublime ideas in the dreamlike, inverted dub architexture of ‘Ion’, settling on mind like a strangely bucolic Incus work on ’Sundry’, and thru the exquisite, tip-toed rhythms of ‘Ecstatic’, to a trippier, bittersweet type of ante-chamber music on ‘Fret (Hear)’.

He’s also deeply charming when left to his own devices. Ambient opener ‘Billow’ calls to mind the tenderness of Cotton Goods works, and ‘Knead’ chases a certain geist of Irdial or Plaid-esque gamelantronica into the sublime title tune, while ‘Prism’ most beautifully ties all his interests in a melting dream sequence which he caps with the harmonic nightlight glow of ‘Column’.
items._genre: experimental / electronic / ambient / microtonal / world fusion
items._cn_summary: Kirk Barley 的《Arc》是其个人创作中的一部完整独奏作品，延续了十年间与 Matthew Herbert 等人合作的脉络，深入探索微分音纯律与另类调弦。专辑在环境电子与实验声响之间展开，以半独奏、半与打击乐手 Matt Davies 合作的形式呈现，融入甘美兰金属敲击、单簧管与吉他，形成流动而松弛的节奏织体。作品兼具民间音乐般的温暖感与未来主义气质，在梦幻的倒置混响结构、细碎切分音型和柔和的旋律片段中推进，从氛围开场到标题曲目，再到以谐波微光收束的结尾，整体连贯而富有层次。Barley 以低调的方式处理复杂调律与不稳定节拍，使音乐在不知不觉中吸引听众，而非强行索取注意力。这张专辑展现了实验电子与跨文化声响融合的独特视角，值得深入聆听。

items.body:
Ambient composer Natalia Beylis leads an ensemble of Nyahh’s finest in her landscape-shaped evocation of a field in Leitrim, Éire, quietly meditating on the natural logic of birds and trees.

‘Around Here The Birds Plant The Trees’ is Beylis’ slow-burn, long-form arrangement for quintet - Eimear Reidy (cello), Tola Custy (fiddle), Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh & Ultan O’Brien (violin), and Willie Stewart (percussion) - seeded in her reading of a blackbird’s dawn chorus, and subsequent conversation with a local farmer on how “birds are the architects of the living landscape”. It follows some 40 solo albums over the past 20 years (not to mention jams with Woven Skull and Tomuttontu) with a considered approach to what lies just beyond her home; typically drawing on her attentive reading of the rural soundsphere to transmute the poetry of birdsong and the natural world into expressive musical metaphor.

The low bowed cello tone of regular spar Eimear Reidy underlines and opens out a breezy space where where the fiddle and violinists criss-cross air in reserved melodic flight and plucky figures that alternate like the play of light on Ireland’s remote North West. The piece unfolds to boggy pockets of percussion and passages of barely-there, hushed gloam, as though the wind itself was generating the players’ gestures, which rise to cloud castle hover around the midway, only to depart for Nyahh label boss Willie Stewart’s rolling drum thunder and scrape of Ailbhe Nic Oireachtaigh's fiddle rooted in the rolling landscape. Ultimately the folk soul of the turf rises in its final section, resembling a rousing, swaying folk song voiced by the strings in ideally creaky discord.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以爱尔兰利特里姆郡的田野为灵感，由环境音乐作曲家 Natalia Beylis 领衔五重奏，将黑鸟晨鸣与农夫所言“鸟类是活景观的建筑师”转化为长篇幅的室内乐式环境作品。音乐在低音大提琴的绵长弓奏中展开，小提琴与中提琴以稀疏旋律和拨弦交错，仿佛光线在西北爱尔兰原野上游移；打击乐如沼泽湿地的闷响，中段渐入云堡般的悬置氛围，随后转向滚雷般的鼓声与琴弓刮擦。终章浮现泥土的民谣灵魂，弦乐以吱哑不协和音汇成摇摆的民间歌谣。整体兼具实验声响与当代古典的细腻，也保留在地民俗气息。

items.body: Heptaméron 七日譚 is an unusually assured debut, one that embraces the vocabulary of progressive rock while refusing to remain within its boundaries. Built around a fantasy narrative structured by the symbolic recurrence of the number seven, the album unfolds like a journey across an imagined landscape of dungeons, mansions, abysses and forgotten kingdoms, each track functioning as a distinct location within a larger world. Rather than simply borrowing fantasy imagery, Acid Brain 酸腦 use it to organise the album’s musical architecture, allowing motifs and textures to recur, mutate and reappear as the story progresses. The opening “…noise (Heptaméron)” eases the listener into this universe with an unexpectedly gentle flute melody recalling classic progressive rock before “Seven Steps Beneath Dungeon” subjects the same material to a sludge-metal transformation that gradually expands into post-rock. Elsewhere, “Into Mansion” continually shifts its internal momentum without losing its hypnotic pull, while the experimental “Gnome (Interlude)” interrupts the narrative with percussion and electronic chaos. The paired “Abyss I” and “Abyss II” anchor the album firmly within stoner rock, one seeming to decay before reassembling itself, the other acting as its distorted mirror. The emotional core of the album is undoubtedly the sixteen-minute “Maru”. LILLIE CREATURES’ ethereal vocals introduce an unexpected shoegaze inflection before gradually taking on an almost incantatory quality as the piece passes through repeated dynamic transformations. The closing “Requiem”, featuring saxophonist Li Zenghui, pushes the album towards free improvisation and noise, ending not with an overwhelming surge of collective energy. Throughout, Acid Brain 酸腦 demonstrate an impressive command of pacing. Their willingness to juxtapose drone, sludge, post-rock, stoner metal, free jazz, electronics and even chiptune could easily have resulted in a fragmented listen, yet the album remains coherent because every stylistic shift serves its fictional geography rather than functioning as a display of eclecticism. The striking cover artwork by yShin perfectly complements this vision. Depicting a humanoid skull fractured into porous, coral-like structures through vivid psychedelic colours and digital distortion, it occupies the same psychedelic territory as the music itself. Anatomy dissolves into abstraction, suggesting both bodily transformation and altered consciousness. Much like the album, the image constantly oscillates between organic and synthetic, decay and regeneration, marking it as a visual extension of the record’s hallucinatory world. Recorded largely in bedrooms and rehearsal spaces with a DIY ethos, Heptaméron 七日譚 never sounds constrained by its circumstances. Instead, Acid Brain 酸腦 transform limited resources into a remarkably ambitious statement. It is a debut that feels fully realised, confidently mapping out a sonic universe whose borders extend well beyond the conventions of heavy psychedelic rock. To get a taste of Acid Brain 酸腦, here is one of their live sets from 2024. Acid Brain 酸腦 are: Shawn Lee 李想 – acoustic guitar, electric guitar, flute, tin whistle, bass, synthesizer, samples, piano, strings, vocals (tracks 1–9), Eric Lai 賴慶禧 – electric guitar (tracks 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9); synthesizer (track 5), Chiayu Hsu 徐嘉佑 – electric guitar, acoustic guitar, synthesizer, samples, vocals (tracks 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9), Yilin Tsai 蔡易霖 – bass, vocals (tracks 2, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9) and Isaac Jiang 江以撒 – drums, percussion (tracks 1–9). To find out more about their album we got in touch directly with them via IG. Heptaméron 七日譚 feels remarkably ambitious for a debut album. Across its nine tracks, you move through drone, stoner rock, post-punk, chiptune, free jazz, post-rock and metal, yet the record never feels like a simple genre exercise. Instead, it unfolds like a coherent fantasy world with its own internal logic. How did the album take shape conceptually, and were there particular books, films, games, myths or musical influences that helped you build this universe of mansions, dungeons, abysses and strange landscapes? From the moment the first song was completed, we decided that this would be a concept album set against a fantasy backdrop. We enjoy embedding symbols within our work, which is why the entire album revolves around the number “7.” The main riff of the opening track is driven by a 7-beat meter, and excluding the intro and interludes, the album consists of exactly seven songs. We are deeply fascinated by the rich world-building in fantasy works, ranging from The Lord of the Rings to The Witcher 3. Influenced heavily by progressive rock concept albums, we wanted to construct a universe of our own. Each track functions like a different location on a vast map, making the entire album a grand tour through this fictional Middle-earth. Although Acid Brain 酸腦 are often described as a heavy psychedelic rock or metal band, Heptaméron 七日譚 incorporates elements that many listeners would not immediately associate with those traditions: flute, tin whistle, synthesizers, chiptune passages, free improvisation and collaborations with artists such as LILLIE CREATURES and Li Zenghui. How did these collaborations come about, and what did those guests bring to the album that you felt could not have been achieved by the band alone? We were completely captivated by Mr. Li Zenghui’s performance when he toured Taipei with Omnipotent Youth Society in 2023. Around that time, he also staged a personal experimental theater piece in Taipei. We fortunately had the opportunity to open for him, which allowed us to extend our invitation. For the album’s finale, “Requiem”, we expanded several sections upon the original foundation to give Mr. Li room to play, and ultimately arranged a free-tempo noise segment, creating what we consider a truly epic ending. We also caught LILLIE CREATURES performing in Taipei once, and we knew we wanted to collaborate with her even before the album was finished. Although we didn’t deliberately tailor the writing to fit her style, the song naturally left space for her. Partnering with her was full of surprises, and we feel incredibly lucky to have her vocals on “Maru”. One of the most striking aspects of the record is the way repetition and transformation operate throughout the album. Pieces such as “Abyss I” and “Abyss II” mirror one another, while “Maru” and “Requiem” continually evolve through changes in instrumentation and texture. Were you consciously thinking in terms of narrative and world-building when composing these pieces, or did the sense of journey emerge naturally from the music itself? Halfway through the writing process (“Seven Steps,” “Mansion,” “Requiem” were finished), we mapped out a complete storyline for the entire album. Ultimately, the narrative and the music influenced each other reciprocally, shaping the final piece into what it is today. Acid Brain 酸腦 emerged from Taipei’s underground music scene with a strong DIY ethos, recording in bedrooms and rehearsal spaces and releasing music on your own terms despite the band’s young age. How would you describe the current underground scene in Taipei, particularly for heavier, experimental or psychedelic music? Do you feel that a new generation of Taiwanese artists is developing its own identity, and what role has that community played in shaping Acid Brain’s sound and outlook? There is a band in Taipei called Bremen Entertainment Inc. They are a heavy psychedelic band and our seniors, who won Album of the Year at our independent music awards. In their acceptance speech, they mentioned that their winning album was also recorded entirely in bedrooms and rehearsal spaces. We loved that idea. In this day and age, everyone should be able to produce the coolest records out of any underground setting with a low-cost approach. (Gianmarco Del Re)
items._genre: progressive rock / experimental / sludge metal / post-rock / free jazz
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以数字七为叙事骨架，构建出一个充满地牢、宅邸、深渊与失落王国的幻想地理。音乐在多种重型与实验风格之间游走，开篇的柔和长笛随后被泥浆金属式的变形吞没，后摇的铺陈与石人摇滚的沉重段落交替出现，自赏式人声在十六分钟的《Maru》中逐渐转为咒语般的吟唱，而结尾曲目则引入萨克斯与自由即兴噪音。尽管素材跨度极大，包括电子声响与芯片音乐，专辑依然凭借对节奏和音色变化的精准控制维持了整体连贯性，每一次风格转换都服务于虚构世界的推进，而非炫耀折衷主义。DIY录制并未限制其野心，封面视觉同样在有机与合成、腐朽与再生之间振荡，与音乐中的幻觉气质互为延伸。

items.body: Intelligent yet playful, We Thought It Was Normal is an assured statement from an artist continuing to refine an already distinctive electronic language. Technical precision with genuine warmth Augusta, Georgia’s Linear North expands an already impressive catalogue with We Thought It Was Normal, a self-released seven-track excursion through IDM, string-inflected house, and richly detailed sampledelia. Equal parts cinematic and rhythmically agile, the release balances technical precision with genuine warmth. “Echo Refuge” opens in contemplative fashion, its expansive atmosphere recalling early The Black Dog before “War Dog Flick” fractures into razor-sharp breakbeat manipulations, neo-funk syncopation, and playful edit work. It reinforces a simple truth: youthful exuberance remains a vital force in contemporary electronic music when guided by mature production instincts. Elsewhere, “Ghost Photo Metro” pairs intricate programming with emotive textures that suggest the human spirit lingering inside digital architecture, while “Brains Nor Backbone” echoes Plaid‘s gift for combining rhythmic sophistication with melodic openness. Every element feels purposeful, never excessive, allowing the compositions to breathe without sacrificing momentum. Closing piece “The Sacred Pattern” introduces an operatic vocal treatment that recalls the theatrical elegance of mid-period Kate Bush, adding an unexpected organic counterpoint to the album’s digital framework. Throughout, We Thought It Was Normal demonstrates that technical fluency needn’t come at the expense of accessibility. Intelligent yet playful, it is an assured statement from an artist continuing to refine an already distinctive electronic language. spaceShift is available on Bandcamp. We Thought It Was Normal by Linear NorthThe post Linear North :: We Thought It Was Normal (Self Released) first appeared on Igloo Magazine.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以精密的节奏编排和温暖的音色构建出兼具电影感与律动性的电子声响。开篇曲目营造出广阔氛围，随后通过锐利的碎拍处理与放克切分展现编辑技巧，既有年轻活力又不失成熟制作意识。多首曲目在复杂编程中融入情感纹理，呼应数字架构中的人性温度，旋律开放性与节奏复杂度并重。结尾加入歌剧式人声，为整体数字框架注入有机质感，形成意外而自然的对比。作品在技术流畅度与可听性之间取得平衡，每个细节都经过精心设计，既不冗赘也不失推进力，展现出艺术家对自身独特电子语言的持续打磨与拓展。

items.album: EMERSON LAKE AND PALMER Emerson Lake and Palmer (Symphonic Prog, 1970)
items.excerpt: Review by Fercandio46 — It is interesting how some people were lucky enough to experience the 70s and see those great bands when they were new, while others of us only learned the history later on; yet, regarding one of the most famous trios, the story is the same for everyone. Carl Palmer came from Atomic Rooster, Keith Emerson from The Nice, and Greg Lake from King Crimson. It was a supergroup with a history that preceded them, much like Cream, even though their music was very different.
items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — It is interesting how some people were lucky enough to experience the 70s and see those great bands when they were new, while others of us only learned the history later on; yet, regarding one of the most famous trios, the story is the same for everyone. Carl Palmer came from Atomic Rooster, Keith Emerson from The Nice, and Greg Lake from King Crimson. It was a supergroup with a history that preceded them, much like Cream, even though their music was very different.Keith Emerson's imprint, his classical influence and innovative adaptations (a signature style he had pioneered with The Nice), combined with a passion for jazz and improvisation, merged with the energy and precision of Carl Palmer. Palmer was a musical sponge, eager to learn and adapt his playing to the demands of the compositions, shifting his style as needed and cementing his legacy as one of the decade's greatest drummers. Then there was the lyricism of Greg Lake, possessor of one of progressive rock's finest voices and a superb bassist, who brought a fascinating, somewhat dark compositional edge from his time in Robert Fripp's band. All of this resulted in something extraordinary, something that took on a life of its own, spiraling beyond their control like a white dove released into the wild."The Barbarian," the album's opening track, is an adaptation of B�la Bart�k's Allegro Barbaro; right from the start, it showcased the group's contemporary edge, sounding modern, daring, and atonal. Keith Emerson demonstrated remarkable versatility and skill, equally adept at tackling classical scores, which he would interpret with wild abandon, and playing the blues on the Hammond organ. Greg Lake's distorted bass work was also a crucial element, helping to craft the dark, theatrical atmosphere of a spectacular debut."Take a Pebble" couldn't get off to a better start, featuring a texture so distinct and sophisticated that it feels like the beginning of a whole new album; Keith brushes the piano strings as if playing a harp, and the cascading piano notes herald one of the band's timeless tracks, a song where hearing the vocals is a delight rediscovered every time one revisits the record. The drum and piano passages respect the vocal phrasing until the instrumental section, driven by a highly fluid bassline, opens the door to jazz, allowing Emerson, Lake & Palmer to excel at what they did best: functioning as a jazz trio, playing at high speed with impeccable timing and groove, yet capable of switching to classical melodies at a moment's notice. After an acoustic passage featuring a rustic guitar style, an improvised section, part classical, part jazz, will follow, before the piece comes full circle to close with the same opening melody. And a finale... truly legendary, between Greg and Keith."Knife-Edge" also gets off to a great start following the end of the previous track; it is a rock song in the trio's signature style (complete with a J.S. Bach quote in the middle) featuring superb accompaniment from Carl Palmer."The Three Fates" begins with a Baroque-evoking pipe organ in "Clotho," the first movement. Then comes "Lachesis", the first of Keith Emerson's piano concertos, shifting from Baroque to jazz; when the drums join in, they create a marvelous pandemonium that breathed new life into music. With the third part, Atropos, reminiscent of Igor Stravinsky. There were excesses, certainly (criticized by many at the time) yet these are precisely what are best remembered and missed from that decade: the artistic excesses that drive history forward. "Tank", fueled by the drums, the inventive bassline, and Keith's furiously played clavinet, also makes for a perfect start following the piano concerto; the entire piece is flawlessly conceived as a cohesive whole. The clavinet improvises with a jazz-like sensibility, despite the classical sound, marking yet another innovation. It showcases the trio at the peak of their powers, including their compositional prowess; everything is meticulously crafted, for after that opening section, a Carl Palmer drum solo paves the way for a historic crescendo featuring Keith on the Mini-Moog.The foot seems to ease off the gas, and the album closes with a ballad that began as a very simple piece, instrumentally enriched by the trio, and has since become an anthem, forming part of the band's DNA in its less experimental guise. That didn't stop Keith from playing around with the Moog at the end of the track, however. Much like King Crimson, it was a stylistically mature debut, featuring an ambitious and rich musical vision that they would only go on to deepen over the course of that first five-year period.

items._cn_summary: 这张ELP的处女作由Keith Emerson、Greg Lake与Carl Palmer组成的三重奏完成，乐评聚焦于其古典与摇滚、爵士的融合。开篇《The Barbarian》改编自巴托克的《Allegro Barbaro》，以不协和音色和现代感确立锋芒；《Take a Pebble》以钢琴拨弦营造精致纹理，随后转入民谣吉他段落与高速爵士三重奏即兴，最终回环至开篇旋律，结构精巧；《Knife-Edge》则引用巴赫，呈现典型的乐队式摇滚语言。乐评强调Emerson对古典素材的即兴化处理、Palmer在不同风格间的精准切换，以及Lake兼具旋律性与暗色气质的嗓音和贝斯演奏。整张专辑在古典曲式、爵士即兴与摇滚能量之间自由游走，三位乐手的个人背景共同塑造了这张具有开创性的前卫摇滚作品。

items.body: Review by svetstawniichuk — I came to Triskaidekaphobie after sitting with Heresie, wanting to hear what Trigaux and Denis did once they left Univers Zero. The title is the fear of the number thirteen, and there is a nod in there to 1313, but the record is not a sequel in costume. Present in 1980 is a leaner, more guitar-driven group. The credited four are Roger Trigaux on guitars and Fender Rhodes, Alain Rochette on Yamaha electric grand piano, Christian Genet on bass, and Daniel Denis on percussion. No bassoon, no viola section. The chamber fog is gone. What remains is rock muscle written with a RIO brain.Three pieces, thirty-eight minutes on the original Atem LP. That length helps. Nothing here needs a second disc to make its point.Promenade au fond d'un canal is the long walk, nearly twenty minutes, and it is the piece I stay for. It works by patterns. A figure repeats, shifts by a small degree, then another figure takes its place. The danger with that method is boredom. Here the band keeps the floor moving. Genet's bass is clear and heavy. Denis does not decorate; every hit seems to lock the next cell in place, then a syncopation shoves the cell forward. Trigaux's guitar starts as part of the pattern and later tears the pattern open with feedback and distortion. The pianos knock rather than prettify. The last stretch is the most physical music I have heard from this Belgian corner: still written, still tight, but finally allowed to howl. Favorite track, without a contest.Quatre-vingt douze is the other long piece, the old side two. The temperature changes. Less hypnotic repetition, more grave, almost classical development, every entrance feeling placed on purpose. I respect it more than I love it on first contact. It can sound strict, even academic, next to the canal walk. After a few sittings I hear the gain: Rochette and Trigaux treating the electric grands as a small orchestra, Genet holding a line that is almost a second argument, Denis staying dry and exact. It is the thinking piece on a record that otherwise wants to corner you.Repulsion is three and a half minutes and does not try to be a fourth symphony. One slow, clinging theme, dressed with gong and cymbal colour from Denis, the group refusing to hurry it into a climax. After two long compositions it works as a last look over the shoulder. I would not start a newcomer here, but I would not cut it either. The album needs that short, haunted full stop.The 2014 Cuneiform disc adds two live tracks from Halles de Schaerbeek, 28 February 1981. I rate the studio three. Compared with Heresie this is less wind-and-string darkness and more electric ensemble writing. Compared with ordinary prog it is still harsh, dissonant, and uninterested in a singable chorus. Four stars: an excellent addition, and for me the right door into Present.Favorite track: Promenade au fond d'un canal.
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Present在1980年的首作，延续了Trigaux与Denis离开Univers Zero后的创作方向，但更强调吉他驱动与电声乐器编排。三首作品共三十八分钟，其中近二十分钟的Promenade au fond d'un canal以重复与微变奏的图案式结构推进，贝斯清晰沉重，鼓组精确锁定节奏，吉他从中段开始以反馈与失真撕裂原有秩序，结尾部分展现出强烈的物理性爆发。Quatre-vingt douze则偏向严肃的古典化发展，两台电钢琴构成小型管弦乐般的对话，贝斯线几乎成为第二旋律，整体气质更冷静克制。Repulsion以三分钟的短小篇幅收束，缓慢的主题配合锣与镲片色彩，形成一种不安的余韵。2014年再版附带两首1981年现场录音。整体上这是一张兼具RIO智性结构与摇滚肌肉感的作品，在保持尖锐不协和的同时，比Heresie更接近电声乐队写作。

items.body: Review by svetstawniichuk — I came to Heresie from the Belgian chamber-rock side of the map rather than from metal or gothic rock. I already knew Univers Zero as a RIO group that writes like a small orchestra with a rhythm section, and this 1979 Atem record is the one people point to when they want the darkest hour of that idea. The sleeve after Bruegel's Triumph of Death is not decoration. It tells you the temperature before a note starts.There are only three pieces on the original LP, and that is enough. Daniel Denis wrote the long opener. Roger Trigaux wrote the two that follow. The credited room is Trigaux on guitar, piano, organ and harmonium, Patrick Hanappier on viola and violin, Michel Berckmans on bassoon and oboe, Guy Segers on bass and voice, and Denis on percussion. No singer in the rock sense. No flute prettying the corners. It is chamber writing that has decided not to comfort you.La Faulx is twenty-five minutes and I will not pretend it is an easy walk. It grows slowly. Early on the air is thick with low harmonium and Berckmans' bassoon, while Segers speaks or chants somewhere behind the instruments rather than standing in front of them. The piece does not rush toward a chorus. It keeps adding weight: strings, reed, percussion that feels ceremonial more than rock. Some nights I stay inside the whole span. Some nights the middle feels long on purpose, like a procession that refuses to hurry. I still come back to it first. If I have to name a favourite, this is the one, because the album's whole climate is already inside those twenty-five minutes.Jack the Ripper is Trigaux's cut, shorter and more pointed. The title does the obvious gothic work, but the music is not a cheap soundtrack joke. Guitar and piano sit closer to the front, Denis gives the drums more of a push, and the counterpoint is easier to follow than the opener. After La Faulx this one feels like the knife instead of the fog. I hear more groove here, more back-and-forth between the players, and I can put it on without needing a whole evening.Vous le Saurez en Temps Voulu closes the original set. Again Trigaux. The title promises that you will know in due time, which fits a record that withholds easy payoffs. This is the piece I reach for when I want the album's colour without the full endurance test of the first side. There are phrases that almost catch, then the group pulls them back into the same grey-green weather. Later Trigaux would take this darker guitar language into Present. You can already hear him leaving the purely chamber frame.I know the 2010 remaster adds Chaos Hermetique, an older 1975 tape with Vincent Motoulle on keys. I stay with the three-track body when I think about a rating. The record is not a masterpiece for every hour of the day. La Faulx can feel monotonous if you came for tunes. Jack and the closer carry more of the argument for repeated plays. Taken as one sitting, though, Heresie is still one of the strongest dark chamber-rock albums I have sat with: sophisticated, dissonant, and honest about its own gloom. Four stars. Excellent, and close enough to essential that I will not bury it in the back of the shelf.Favorite track: La Faulx.

items._cn_summary: 这张1979年的专辑以室内乐编制与摇滚节奏结合，呈现暗黑而仪式感的声响。原作LP仅三首曲目：开篇《La Faulx》长达25分钟，低音管、簧风琴与弦乐缓慢叠加，人声隐于器乐之后，营造出压抑的进行曲质感；《Jack the Ripper》更短促直接，吉他与钢琴靠前，鼓点推动出类似刀锋的紧张对位；《Vous le Saurez en Temps Voulu》延续灰绿色调，旋律刚有轮廓便被拉回晦暗氛围。乐评指出，这张专辑并非随时可听的悦耳之作，其单调感在长曲中尤为明显，但正是这种拒绝妥协的室内乐写作，使其成为暗色前卫摇滚领域的代表。2010年再版附加的早期录音未被计入核心评价。

items.body: Chicago poet and performer Marvin Tate presents vivid vignettes of magic and loss on his elusive new album, writes Mosi Reeves in The Wire 511 Marvin Tate Controlled Burn Amalgam DL/LP Marvin Tate is a linchpin of Chicago’s creative arts scene, emerging as a slam poet in the early 1990s and subsequently participating in an array of musical and literary endeavours, from jazz funk ensembles like Uptighty (which included future members of Tortoise) to 2025’s avant jazz foray Andreas Røysum Ensemble With Marvin Tate. In a 1998 profile, the alt weekly Chicago Reader described his unusual voice as “high and fast paced with rich undertones, like a Fat Albert cartoon character crossed with Screamin’ Jay Hawkins and a little bit of Martin Luther King Jr”. Tate himself has cited Gwendolyn Brooks and Amiri Baraka as chief influences. Aficionados of the jazzoetry world may draw comparisons to the ragged blues Melvin Van Peebles once conjured on 1968’s Brer Soul. However, none of that is preparation for Controlled Burn, which matches Tate’s springy, salty tenor with shifting backdrops or no music at all. It’s a collaboration with instrumentalist and producer LeRoy Bach, who has worked with Tate since their membership of Uptighty. But Controlled Burn is hardly a Black blues meets alt culture mash-up. Bach’s arrangements, made with help from drummer Quin Kirchner and flautist Ben LaMar Gay, sit behind Tate as he speaks haltingly yet deliberately. It feels like they are adjusting to his worldview, not the other way around, and the songs they create feel deeply lived in instead of a one-off studio novelty. The resulting pieces may not be as immersive as Tate’s work with Andreas Røysum Ensemble, but they draw closer attention to the way he plays with words and persona. “Baller” appears to be an autobiographical reminiscence of Tate’s dead brother. “My brother was a baller, taught me one-on-one, beat me in a foot race in the presence of a gun”, he intones. “Damn judge gave him seven… the streets gave him life”. As the 28 minute album unfolds, it becomes clear that Tate is writing characters that may or not be inspired by his real life. Many of his pieces take unusual twists and don’t adhere to a rhyme pattern. “Darren” begins as a lament for an old lover and ends with a memory of a conversation he once had: “Hey Darren, you ever waterboarded? How does that feel, Darren?”. The number unfolds over a filtered guitar riff as if Tate is talking to someone in a concert hall while a band play onstage. “First You Hear” is swathed in punk noise that evokes the metallic dirges of Black Flag circa My War. Meanwhile, Tate seems to adopt a young man’s swagger for “Genius Shit” as he says, “Tragedy starts in the mind first, death is only imminent if all else falls”. “Love Bass (I Was Hoping)” is another cut about romance expired as he rues, “That poly thing never worked out for us/Too many opinions and illogic over practicality”. Throughout, Tate finds ways to dramatically shift the meaning of his songs. “She never cared for your race play”, he says as he ends “Hold Me”. Another example is the final line on “Love Bass (I Was Hoping)” where he asks, “If love is the answer, then why are we still asking the same questions?”. Tate’s slipperiness as a narrator is countered by a crusted, raspy tone that can shift from an odd squeal, like when he yelps “Free!” on “Best Side” to the gospel croon he uses for the a cappella track “Robin” as he sings, “I hope you miss me when I’m gone”. The halting way he delivers his pieces and the formatting of the songs ensure that much of Controlled Burn is enveloped in silence, allowing the listener to briefly meditate over his verses. Bach, for his part, devises music that enhances Tate’s uniqueness as a performer while subtly upending expectations, whether it’s the riffing guitar loop of “Darren” or the warm Boards Of Canada-like electronics of “Genius Shit”. Not every gambit works – the vibe-y beat of “Mosh Pit” sounds a bit too much like middling downtempo. But Bach’s overall approach ensures that Controlled Burn is intriguingly difficult to categorise. When encountering Tate’s confident, assured delivery, one can’t help but wonder why he hasn’t received greater attention despite the best efforts of Chicago indie royalty like Joan Of Arc’s Tim Kinsella and singer-songwriter Angel Olsen (who released a pretty and sincere homage to him in 2013, Tim Kinsella Sings The Songs Of Marvin Tate By Leroy Bach Featuring Angel Olsen). For certain, Tate’s name has begun to pop up outside of the Windy City: he made cameos on the late jazz trumpeter jaimie branch’s 2019 album Fly Or Die II: Bird Dogs Of Paradise as well as Corinne Bailey Rae’s iconoclastic 2023 effort Black Rainbows. Perhaps Controlled Burn will introduce his work to a much deserved wider audience. This review appears in The Wire 511 along with many other reviews of new and recent records, books, films, festivals and more. To read them all, pick up a copy of the magazine in our online shop. Wire subscribers can also read the issue in our online magazine library.
items._cn_summary: 芝加哥诗人Marvin Tate与制作人LeRoy Bach合作的专辑，以诗歌朗诵为核心，配以爵士、噪音和极简编排。Tate的嗓音高亢急促，带着丰富质感，在无音乐或零散器乐背景下，讲述关于死亡、记忆与街头生活的片段。作品不依赖传统韵律，叙事常出人意料，如《Darren》从旧爱悼念转向水刑拷问的对话，《First You Hear》被朋克噪音包裹，呼应Black Flag的阴郁声响。整张专辑28分钟，仿佛诗人在排练厅或音乐会现场即兴言说，乐队跟随其节奏而非相反，营造出深沉的生活气息。相比Tate与Andreas Røysum乐队的合作，这里更聚焦于他本人的文字游戏与角色扮演，在实验爵士与口语诗之间找到独特交汇点。

items.body: Band: Papangu | Album: Celestial | Genre: Progressive rock, Jazz-rock | Year: 2026 From: João Pessoa, Brazil | Label: Deck For fans of: Genesis, Soft Machine, Gentle Giant, King Crimson Bandcamp Brazilian prog quintet Papangu returns with their third LP, Celestial. This was likely my most-anticipated album of the year, given this group’s track record. Their 2021 debut, Holoceno, is, to date, the only album I’ve given a perfect score to upon release. That album is easily the best integration of zeuhl and metal I’ve heard, and even now it absolutely holds up after many, many listens. Then in 2024, the band shifted their sound rather drastically on their sophomore LP Lampião Rei. With the expansion of the band to include keyboards and wind instruments, Papangu explored a jazzier direction. That jazziness continues here, with sounds from both the band’s native Brazil and the Canterbury scene playing prominent roles. Hints and dashes of their metal and zeuhl roots crop up throughout this album, but the sound is overall much closer to Lampião Rei than to the apocalyptic tones of Holoceno. Overall, I enjoy Celestial a lot. Papangu demonstrates a fantastic ability to incorporate forró music from their native northeastern Brazil in a way that feels completely organic. This is especially prominent on “Bode Expiatório”, where triangle and flute work opposite some fantastically wonky synth tones, and on “Fechamento de Corpo”, where it marries with ethereal space rock. But even more so than their incorporation of Brazilian music, the most dominant flavors here (outside progressive rock, obviously) are various strains of jazz. Every song on Celestial could be described as “jazzy,” but there is a lot of variation between cuts. Some moments are light and relaxed, like “Afirmação”, and others are tauter, such as “Iamanakaru”. Keyboards dominate the sound palette of Celestial, which largely serves to underscore the band’s jazzy turn. Swirling organ, tinkling electric piano, and intergalactic synths all mingle and weave around each other to create lush soundscapes. Just because Papangu has largely pivoted away from the sounds of Holoceno doesn’t mean that there are no commonalities between it and this album. I wouldn’t call any songs on this record “metal,” but a few have passages that flirt with being metallic. “Taxidermia” is the overall-heaviest song on the album, and “Calado (do Olho)” spotlights some tangled, zeuhlish riffage. Zeuhl-inspired moments crop up elsewhere, too. “Celeste” features some moments that clearly draw from Magma, and the chanting on “Iamanakaru” wouldn’t be out of place on a Corima record. Harsh vocals are used a handful of times throughout the album, to somewhat mixed results. The growled backing vocals on the opening “Mau-Olhado” come off as awkward in an otherwise-solid song. But their deployment in “Taxidermia” feels more effective. Another ding against this album is that the guitars can feel pretty thin and unimpactful. This is not universal. There absolutely are moments where the guitars sound great, but on some tracks—especially the first two on the album—there is a lack of depth. Compare this to the keyboards, which consistently sound phenomenal. I do need to compliment the way this album is put together. Each of the individual songs flow naturally, and they all feel the appropriate length. I don’t think Papangu has yet recorded a song that has felt overlong, which is a rare feat for a prog band on their third LP. And at a macro level, the record is very well-paced and feels satisfying. Celestial makes sense for Papangu’s trajectory. They leaned hard into jazz and Brazilian music on their last album, and they’ve doubled down here. Everything is very smartly assembled, and the band members demonstrate keen instrumental skills. I am glad they’re forging their own path and following their artistic hearts. That said, I do miss their heavier sound, as well as the former prominence of zeuhl. But with this band, you never quite know what you’re going to get next. Score: 86/100

items._cn_summary: 巴西前卫摇滚五人组帕潘古的第三张专辑延续了上一张的爵士化转向，键盘（管风琴、电钢琴、合成器）成为主导，营造出稠密而通透的声响层次。与巴西东北部传统音乐的结合尤为自然，三角铁、长笛与怪诞合成器音色相互穿插，也将太空摇滚、泽乌尔式段落和少量金属质感融入其中。专辑在松弛与紧绷之间切换：有的曲目轻盈放松，有的以密集的吟唱和扭曲连复段推进；清嗓与嘶吼的搭配并非处处理想，吉他的厚度也略显不足。整体上，这是一张以爵士摇滚为骨架、融合地域音乐与坎特伯雷风味的作品，适合关注前卫/融合走向的听众。

items.body:
STROOM fills in a gap on the timeline, excavating vital experiments made in Cologne in the wake of the cult 'Novaya Scena' compilation by Svitlana Nianio, Michael Springer, Guido Erfen, Soloveyka, Yewgeny Taran and Wolfram Burgtorf.

Back in 1993, a bizarre 20-track compilation appeared from Cologne's musical fringe. The idea for the set had come from artist and producer Erfen and sound engineer and percussionist Springer, two close friends who, taking advantage of cheap rent and disused buildings, put on regular events and established a recording studio in their neighborhood, off the beaten track. Erfen was a dedicated tape trader and had received a transmission from Kharkiv's Novaya Scena rock club that arrived with an essay and music from three local bands. At this time, Ukraine was still under Soviet rule and the music fascinated the two friends, shining a spotlight on a part of the world they were completely unfamiliar with. When singer and keyboardist Soloveyka visited cologne a year later, she handed Erfan more tantalizing music, inspiring him to make his own pilgrimage to Ukraine to investigate further. The research resulted in the 'Novaya Scene' CD, a set of tracks recorded between 1986 and 1992 that muddled prog with new wave, punk, folk and avant-garde rock. It was released on Hamburg's What's So Funny About label and was supposed to have a sequel.

That's where 'Aftermath and Transitions' comes in. Following the release of 'Novaya Scena', Erfen and Springer set up a series of sessions at their studio, inviting some of the Ukrainian artists to record with them. It's this period that resulted in Svitlana Nianio's 'Transilvania Smile' soundtrack that was properly released for the first time on Muscat sublabel Shukai in 2023. Nianio had been a member of Cukor Bila Smerť (the band who'd provided the stylistic anchor for 'Novaya Scena') and took the opportunity to launch her solo career, with Springer working as engineer. And there was more material from those sessions that Springer held back: the compilation's first four tracks are collaborations between Nianio, Springer, Taran and Springer's good friend Burgtorf. Opener 'Fake' was almost finished when Nianio showed up at the studio with her Casio in tow, so Springer plugged her in and she ended up lavishing the beat with vocals in Ukrainian and oddball keyboard vamps. The other three tracks were a little more organic, improvised in the studio while the artists got familiar with one another - there's the decelerated reggae experiment 'ManySpace', the instrumental groover 'Quiet Place' and best of all 'Політ Світляки', a wiry percussive jam that's not aged a day.

Erfen joins in on the ace exotica-tinged 'Whispering Walls' and 'Tired River', tracks from the group's final session in 1995. Nianio and Taran were planning to renew their visas and return to Cologne to record more, but it never happened - the recordings were shelved and the artists went about their lives independently. Then there's the three Solar tracks recorded by Soloveyka and Burgtorf who struck up a friendship after meeting at Springer's studio. Singing in Russian and English, Soloveyka breathes cabaret energy over Burgtorf's jerky, sample-heavy ethno-groove productions. And it's left to Taran to finish things off, with a "1996 Version" of his 'Death and the Bachelor' track that features none other than Nianio on keys. Phew. It's a brilliant set, really - not just one for STROOM obsessives, it'll speak to anyone whose interest in the Ukrainian underground was piqued by 'Transilvania Smile' or Muscut's ace Cukor Bila Smerť anthology.

items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了1994至1996年间乌克兰音乐人在科隆留下的录音，源自《Novaya Scena》之后的一系列工作室即兴与合作。参与者包括Svitlana Nianio、Michael Springer、Guido Erfen等，他们将后苏联时期的乌克兰地下场景与西欧实验语境相接。曲目既有Nianio用Casio键盘和乌克兰语人声叠加的节拍，也有即兴生成的减速雷鬼、打击乐合奏与异域情调氛围。这批母带曾被搁置多年，如今以合辑形式重见天日，呈现了东欧与德国实验音乐之间一段被忽视的交叉历史。

items.body:
Mika Vainio & Ilpo Väisänen’s first ever release as Panasonic, originally issued in 1994 as the "Panasonic EP", a while before they were forced by the electronic goods coroporation of the same name to drop the A...

A real slice of history right here, presenting longer and harder versions of a cut that appeared in a shorter form on Mika’s Ø album ‘Metri’, co-credited to him and Ilpo, and here going longer and doubled up with another duo battering ram, ‘Murtaja’. Both tunes sound very much of their time, when European techno was forged tougher to demand, paralleling movements of harder Chicago house and Detroit warehouse techno.

In Panasonic’s case, the results were typically ascetic, mostly bleached of discernible melody beyond rhythmelodic cadence, and locked, bloody-minded, to icy tattoos that reflected their origins in Finnish warehouse parties, and would pin them on the international techno and electronic music maps. Trust that ‘Muuntaja’ still leaves welts from its distorted kicks, and contains subs primed to quake foundations, whilst the B-side is ideal for gnashing rave punks and bass drum fetishists.
items._cn_summary: 这张1994年首发的EP是Panasonic（Mika Vainio与Ilpo Väisänen）最早的作品，后因同名电器公司被迫改名。其中《Muuntaja》是Mika在Ø专辑《Metri》中一首短作的加长加硬版，并与另一首《Murtaja》构成双曲目冲击。两首曲目带有鲜明的90年代欧洲技术乐特征，回应更硬的芝加哥house与底特律仓库techno脉络。声音处理极度克制，几乎剥离旋律，只保留节奏性韵律与冰冷、固执的律动；失真底鼓和低频震动具有强烈的物理压迫感，B面则更偏向锐舞朋克与低音鼓迷恋者。作品源自芬兰仓库派对场景，也奠定了他们在国际techno与电子音乐版图上的位置。

items.body:
All killer, no filler trotters from a golden period of Lee ‘Scratch’ Perry’s foundational work at fabled studio, The Black Ark.

This 3rd in a prized series spies the wee madman conjuring multidimensional spectres from vocal recordings of regular spars: Max Romeo, The Jolly Brothers, Leroy Sibbles, The Mistic, and Devon Irons. Perry’s visionary, innovative application of studio-as-instrument tekkerz come to the fore in the music’s layered diffusions, which we may take for granted in contemporary music, but was radical back then, and whose uncanny appeal has only steeped with age. 

Including a solo standout in the ghostly, harmonised roots wooze of his ‘Dread Lion’ gem as King Scratch, it spans the signature, lysergic sparkle of his ‘Conscious Man’cut with The Jolly Brothers, thru a stepping 12” mix of Max Romeo’s ‘Norman’ (1978), and heat-hazed sway to Leroy Sibbles’ ‘Garden of Life’, along with The Mistic’s eyes-down devotional ‘Forward With Jah’, and sloshing nyabingi of ‘When Jah Comes’ for Devon Irons.
items._genre: dub / reggae / roots reggae / experimental / world
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑收录了Lee Perry在Black Ark录音室黄金时期的五首经典混音，展现他将录音室本身作为乐器的前卫手法。Perry从Max Romeo、The Jolly Brothers等合作者的原始人声中提取素材，通过分层扩散、相位调制与空间化处理，营造出多重维度的声响幻象。这种制作技术在当年极为激进，其诡异而迷人的质感随时间推移愈发醇厚。曲目涵盖King Scratch署名下的《Dread Lion》中幽灵般的和声根音乐氛围，The Jolly Brothers版本《Conscious Man》标志性的迷幻光泽，Max Romeo《Norman》的12寸步进混音，Leroy Sibbles《Garden of Life》的热浪摇曳感，以及The Mistic和Devon Irons作品中的虔诚低垂与nyabinghi节奏律动。整张合辑既是牙买加dub美学的集中体现，也是实验录音技术与世界音乐传统交汇的范例。
