items.body: Darkwave and synthwave duo Dead Astronauts release their fifth studio album, “Shallow Grave“, on 2 October 2026 through Cold Transmission Music. The album appears on digital and on CD in a 6-panel digipak with a lyrics booklet. Two gatefold vinyl editions follow on 9 October, each pressed in a run of 150 copies, one on solid white and one on solid orange. When Side-Line covered the first single in July, no release date had been announced. The label has now pinned the date, the formats and the running order. Ten tracks make up the record: “An Intro”, “Bodies”, “Shallow Grave”, “Get Lost”, “Glistening Things”, “Who Kills Who”, “Stuck (In a Modern Day Cult)”, “Make It Right”, “From Dust” and a “Dark Club Version” of “Bodies”. The vinyl carries the same ten tracks across two sides. Dead Astronauts wrote and produced the album themselves; it was mixed and mastered at Influx Studios in Bern, where duo member Slade Templeton works as an engineer, and the art and design come from JthreeConcepts, the studio run by his bandmate Jared Kyle Nickerson. Shallow Grave by Dead Astronauts The duo describe the album as a record about disconnection, obsession and mortality: “Dark, melodic and occasionally abrasive, Shallow Grave pulls from darkwave, synthwave and post-punk without settling comfortably into any one of them. Beneath the syrupy drone and distortion, it’s a record about being human in an increasingly strange world – and the uncomfortable realization that none of us in our current state are getting out of it alive.” Dead Astronauts release a visualizer for ‘Bodies’ A visualizer for “Bodies” went up on the Cold Transmission Music channel on 14 August 2026. The track opens the album proper after the instrumental “An Intro” and returns at the end in its Dark Club Version. The album’s first single, “Get Lost”, came out on 26 June 2026 with a video the same day; Side-Line covered it in Dead Astronauts release video for ‘Get Lost’, first single from ‘Shallow Grave’. About Dead Astronauts Dead Astronauts began in late 2011 as a project of digital illustrator Jared Kyle Nickerson, who records as Jared Kyle. Hayley Stewart joined in early 2012 and sang on the debut album “Constellations”, released digitally on 16 October 2014. “Arms of Night” followed on 11 November 2016 through NewRetroWave, mastered by Slade Templeton, with a clear vinyl edition in February 2017 and two further limited pressings in April 2022. Stewart later left to concentrate on her solo project Mecha Maiko. The band moved to Cold Transmission Music with the single “Forgetting Me” on 28 October 2020, backed with a Mecha Maiko remix. The album “Silhouettes” arrived on 15 January 2021 and the remix set “Silhouettes Redux” on 3 December 2021, with reworks from SYZYGYX, Ultra Sunn, Mecha Maiko and Crying Vessel. Florence Bullock of Los Angeles handled vocals and lyrics across that run and last appeared as a guest on “The Red Dress” on the fourth album, ‘Ghosts’, issued on 26 April 2024. The band now operates as the duo of Kyle, based in Seattle, and Templeton, based in Bern. Their most recent release before the new album cycle was the benefit single “Yuu Yuu” on 5 December 2025, recorded with Kakuma Sound and supporting musicians at the Kakuma refugee camp in Kenya. “Shallow Grave” is their third full album for Cold Transmission Music.
items._cn_summary: Dead Astronauts的第五张专辑《Shallow Grave》延续了暗潮与合成器浪潮的融合路线，并加入后朋克的棱角。乐队自称作品围绕疏离、执念与死亡展开，在粘稠的嗡鸣与失真中呈现人性在陌生世界中的处境。专辑包含十首曲目，以器乐引子开场，同名曲与主打曲《Bodies》贯穿首尾，并收录其暗黑俱乐部混音版。制作上由双人组自行完成创作与制作，混音母带在伯尔尼的Influx Studios进行，视觉设计出自成员Jared Kyle Nickerson的工作室。发行由独立厂牌Cold Transmission Music负责，提供CD与限量彩胶格式。整体上这是一张风格混合、氛围阴暗的暗潮作品，适合偏好合成器质感和后朋克节奏的听众。

items.body: Italian darkwave and cold post-punk project iamnoone release their fifth album, “Gloomy Days“, on 4 September 2026 through Cold Transmission Music. The digital edition arrives first; a CD in a 6-panel digipak, limited to 300 copies, follows on 2 October. Thirteen tracks run for 58 minutes, four of them produced in collaboration with Greek producer Kay-Chi. The duo of Philippe Marlat (vocals, baritone guitar, synthesizer) and Stephan Seth (bass, backing vocals, synthesizer) mix classic dark wave with cold post-punk, layering baritone guitar and hypnotic synth lines under Marlat’s low vocal register. Marlat mixed and mastered the album at LMD music studio, with Morgan Fussli as production assistant, and also supplied the artwork and photography. Gloomy Days by iamnoone The tracklist runs “a season in hell (feat. Kay-Chi)”, “gloomy days”, “F.O.M.T”, “a box of tears”, “in our time of dying”, “torture (feat. Kay-Chi)”, “still awake”, “never leave, never die”, “into the void (feat. Kay-Chi)”, “sweet loneliness”, “I come undone”, “astral fall” and “one out, one in (feat. Kay-Chi)”. The band describe the record as a study in stalled time rather than despair: “Days when the sun fails to rise upon the earth and within our hearts. Days when all hope seems lost. Endless days, made of time slipping away too fast or far too slow. […] Let us taste and embrace the solitude and the stillness that these days bring forth.” iamnoone bring in Kay-Chi across four tracks Kay-Chi, an Athens-based producer also signed to Cold Transmission Music, plays synthesizer and electronics on “a season in hell”, “torture”, “into the void” and “one out, one in”. His own catalogue includes the “Night Protocol” EP and the album “Brighter Shadows”, plus remix work for the label. Two of those collaborations arrived ahead of the album. “a season in hell” came out as a single on 12 June 2026 with a video released the same week, and “into the void” followed on 3 July 2026. Both clips were directed by iamnoone and published on the Cold Transmission Music channel. A third video, for “F.O.M.T”, was announced in July and is credited to Stephan Seth and Philippe Marlat. About iamnoone iamnoone is the project of Philippe Marlat, who also records under his birth name Filippo Galleani, and Stephan Seth. The pair are based in Italy and describe their own territory as cold wave, dark wave and occult wave. Their account of the band’s origin is deliberately spare: “Sometimes, a path one chooses, crosses another path chosen by a like-minded person. iamnoone was born at one of these crossroads.” The first release was the six-track EP “DVPLEX” on 17 March 2019. Cold Transmission Music issued the debut album “A Primitive Trinitas” on 29 February 2020 as a CD in a 6-panel digipak, recorded and produced at the duo’s own la maison diev. “Dead Season” followed on 26 November 2021 on digital and CD, with a white vinyl edition on 4 March 2022, and the nine-track ‘Together Alone’ on 6 January 2023. ‘The Joy of Sorrow’, twelve tracks, arrived on 4 October 2024, again written, recorded and mixed at la maison diev and mastered by Pete Burns at The Shelter. The three-track single “MFM”, which included a remix by Ermete Lo Stige, came out on 25 July 2025, and the six-track companion EP “melancholia” on 5 December 2025 in a run of 100 hand-printed, numbered and wax-sealed copies. Side-Line spoke to the duo in February 2025 for the feature Interview with Iamnoone: ‘Darkness Is A Natural Element Of Life And Should Be Understood’. “Gloomy Days” is their fifth album for Cold Transmission Music and the first on which a labelmate shares production duties.
items._cn_summary: iamnoone的第五张专辑《Gloomy Days》包含十三首曲目，总长58分钟，其中四首与希腊制作人Kay-Chi合作。乐队以男中音吉他、贝斯、合成器与低音域人声构建声响，称专辑探讨的是停滞的时间而非绝望，强调在漫长灰暗日子中拥抱孤独与静止。Marlat负责混音与母带处理，并参与视觉创作。专辑通过Cold Transmission Music发行，先出数字版，后出限量CD，并已发布多支单曲及视频。

items.body:
Smiling C trail their Shams Dinn diamond with this bounty of Washington Go-Go picks from the short-lived Aset label’s Whax, Treo, and Latonya, all recorded and originally released c. 1986-88. Like the Shams LP, A Totally New Sound brims with pure soulful optimism and home-baked charm, but rather than early Arabic rap and ‘80s boogie, this one surveys a blindspot in most collections with some of the rarest and most special Go-Go Records in existence. 

All eight song were written by the Aset label’s in-house players, revolving song-writers Mbu Mbulu and O Jabbo, and includes their semi-released instrumental Skip, along with three beauties by the 11 year old singer Latonya which are almost worth entry alone, plus one wild one by the Whax duo, and three from Treo, the trio of Cathy Young, Delores Lidell and Linda Lawson.

Seriously, the Latonya tracks are what pop dreams are made of - precocious yet innocent, flush with colourful melodies and driven by that bustling Go-Go hustle, the super infectious Dance Time is a ready-made anthem, while Eyes Of A Child and We Will Teach The Adults weirdly also recall early ‘80s Belgian cold wave crossed with Langley Schools Music Project, or something.

The Aset Players’ Skip reveals the boogie mechanics under their pop hood, while Whax tend to the freakier side with a spot of Rick James-ian flair, and Treo’s close harmonies come out perfectly pop-wise in Demands Demands Demands, but Second Is Too Close and the forlorn romance of When Your Love Is Gone feels too weird to be pop proper, and that’s where the magick lies in this LP, between Aset’s mainstream ambition and a realness of expression that can’t be missed.
items._cn_summary: 这张合辑由华盛顿阿塞特厂牌整理，收录瓦克斯、特雷奥与拉托尼亚等艺人在一九八六至一九八八年间录制的稀有戈戈舞曲，全部作品出自厂牌内部创作核心之手。十一岁的拉托尼亚贡献的三首曲目尤为突出，早熟又天真的嗓音与色彩鲜明的旋律，在戈戈律动中呈现出类似早期比利时冷潮与兰利学校音乐计划的古怪质感；瓦克斯偏向放克怪诞，特雷奥的密集和声在流行与疏离之间摇摆。器乐曲《跳跃》则显露出流行外壳下的布吉机制。整张唱片在主流流行野心与真实、笨拙的表达之间形成独特张力。

Marquinn Mason’s vocals elevate the session to classiest lounge club levels, dusting a jazz-soul flow to the Brazilian shuffle of ‘Bossa Beat’, and oiling the broken beat angularity of ‘Bounce’, before ideally adapting to the squashed electro-soul boogie of ‘Moving Steady’, and reminding of Omar-S joints with John F.M. ben Hixon’s remix only accentuates that comparison with a supple ATL-via-313-and-NYC Salsoul deep house appeal.

items.body:
For anyone paying attention to Vietnamese or Cambodian pop culture, the past several days have seen a flurry of online commentary in Southeast Asia and beyond about a new music video by Phương Mỹ Chi and DTAP titled 'Thiên đường với người thương', or 'Paradise with my love'. The track is in Vietnamese and follows the conventions of Vietnamese pop, but the music video (MV) features Khmer Krom culture from southern Vietnam, with scenes filmed at Khmer wats (temples), displays of Khmer dance, and a staging of a Khmer wedding. The central characters in the video are a classical dancer, played by Phương Mỹ Chi, and a musician, played by actor Bảo Định, who meet as children, grow up together, fall in love, and get married.

The video presents a wholesome story and celebrates Khmer Krom culture. The Khmer Krom, or lower Khmer, live in the Mekong Delta and are related to the Khmer people of Cambodia. Both were once part of the Khmer Empire, but several factors have shaped a distinct Khmer Krom culture. Starting in the 17th century, Vietnamese populations moved into the Mekong Delta, which ushered in several centuries of cultural mixture. French colonisation and independence movements established a boundary between Cambodia and southern Vietnam that limited movement. And the distinct qualities of the Mekong Delta itself yielded new cultural forms. The Khmer Krom therefore have many folk traditions about which little is known.

Responses to the video have largely been positive, but it has touched a nerve among some netizens who decry the cultural appropriation of Khmer culture by a Vietnamese pop artist. This debate offers insight into the wider geopolitics of Southeast Asia and the trends of contemporary pop in Vietnam.

The release of 'Thiên đường với người thương' has taken place amid vibrant experimentation with folk traditions in Vietnamese popular music. Songs of folk pop or folktronica feature pop singers reclaiming various folk traditions of their parents and grandparents to fuse them with popular music models that circulate worldwide. Phương Mỹ Chi has several tracks that blend southern Vietnamese traditional music with global pop aesthetics. Artists from northern Vietnam do the same: Hoàng Thùy Linh's 'Để Mị Nói Cho Mà Nghe' incorporates elements of Hmong music, and Kiều Anh's 'Lá Ngọc Cành Vàng' folds a short ca trù (sung poetry) tune into an instrumental interlude.

At the same time, the Vietnamese government plays an influential role both publicly and behind the scenes in promoting some artists over others. For instance, in 2013, the government banned public lip-synching to promote genuine vocal performance but later rescinded the ban. More recently, several pop musicians, including Miu Lê and Phương Diễm Huyền, faced criminal prosecution for supposed illegal activity. Any arrest is a warning to other singers, as Vietnamnet recently indicated.

In this context, Vietnamese pop artists must figuratively walk several tightropes in their artistic creation. The first tightrope involves navigating the razor-edged distinction between cultural appropriation and legitimate experimentation in an environment of fickle social media trends and youth tastes. On this, 'Thiên đường với người thương' has done rather well.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by VietQ Media (@vietqmedia)

An article in Cambodia-based The Phnom Penh Post suggests that the music video appropriately “acknowledges” the origins of the Khmer dance and rituals. This echoes Cambodian and Khmer Krom social media posts that relay a sense of pride in seeing Khmer culture represented on an international stage. Vietnamese and diasporic Vietnamese communities also enjoy the video, as VietQ Media has reported.

Social media posts strengthened the case for visual acknowledgement one day after the MV’s release. Phương Mỹ Chi gave her thanks to Trà Vinh University and her dance teacher, Thạch Thị Út Linh, while DTAP released a visual of musical instruments and customs seen in the music video.

The track has not been entirely successful in raising awareness of Khmer Krom sonic culture, however. During one instrumental interlude, for instance, the MV shows musicians playing various instruments of the Khmer classical music genre pinpeat, or ngũ âm in Vietnamese, including the sralai (a quadruple-reed instrument) and Bảo Định playing the roneat ek (xylophone). But the soundtrack contains none of the distinct timbres of these instruments. Instead, listeners hear a rather boring guitar riff. Khmer culture is seen here but not heard.

The second tightrope involves navigating opaque areas of government permissibility. I have no access to specific information about the making of the MV, but the video's wide circulation suggests that it meets government regulations and requirements. The song also upholds the ideals of the recent Resolution 80 on the development of cultural industries in Vietnam, which seeks to promote culture but also manage it appropriately.

Given this environment, it’s no small feat to find fertile middle ground between artistry and policy to successfully represent Khmer culture in Vietnam. This is of paramount importance because of the difficulties today in accessing Khmer Krom music, dance, and rituals. Artists do not often perform outside of the Mekong Delta, with only a handful of performances taking place every year in large cities in Vietnam. Tourists also rarely visit Khmer communities in southern Vietnam, given the lack of infrastructure.

At the same time, murky restrictions often prevent the study of Khmer arts in southern Vietnam. Earlier this year, the very university that supported the MV’s production team would not authorise my Khmer music lessons with staff instructors. This is, of course, the university’s prerogative, and given the long history of colonial and other forms of exploitation, I understand their caution. But my case is not an isolated one among domestic and foreign researchers in Vietnam. And might the commercial use of the Khmer arts by a Vietnamese pop singer also be seen as a form of exploitation?

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Phương Mỹ Chi (@phuongmychi)

The case of 'Thiên đường với người thương' is therefore a complicated one. The song acknowledges, represents, and values the Khmer arts in Vietnam, but at the same time manages and exploits them for commercial and nationalistic ends. But no government can fully control a narrative.

Among the online discussion are several commentators from Thailand who have both congratulated Vietnam for displaying “Thai culture” — thereby completely erasing Khmer and Khmer Krom culture — and remonstrated with Vietnam for featuring “inauthentic” forms of Thai costume and dance. In the midst of a military conflict between Cambodia and Thailand, they have added to the widening culture war between the two countries by bringing Vietnam into it.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Ben Pham (@bnphm0609)

Pop is never boring, and foreign (i.e. non-Southeast Asian) audiences must start to pay attention to the dynamics that bring these songs to life. 'Thiên đường với người thương' encourages reflection on the interconnected nature of music and everyday life and the shifting tightropes that all individuals must navigate when making artistic decisions. And while certain powers may attempt to control a narrative, the openness of the Internet quickly dissolves that enclosure.

I am therefore optimistic about 'Thiên đường với người thương'. I truly hope that it will generate new interest in Khmer Krom culture and open new doors for Khmer artists to showcase their artistry to new audiences. The paradise of the video, then, may not be romantic love, but may instead be a paradise of visibility. Audibility may well be next.

Written by Alexander M. Cannon. He is Professor of Ethnomusicology at the University of Birmingham. This article benefited from a conversation with an avid consumer of Vietnamese popular culture who wishes to remain anonymous. Their contribution is gratefully acknowledged.

items._cn_summary: Phương Mỹ Chi与DTAP的这支MV以越南流行音乐为基底，融合南部高棉族群的传统文化元素，包括寺庙场景、高棉舞蹈与婚礼仪式。歌曲本身遵循主流流行结构，但视觉与主题上对Khmer Krom文化的呈现具有明确的地区指向性。文章指出该作品处于越南当代流行音乐复兴民间传统的浪潮中，类似Hoàng Thùy Linh等艺人将少数民族音乐元素融入流行框架的做法。MV引发关于文化挪用的争议，也折射出东南亚地缘政治与越南政府对流行音乐的管控背景。整体上这是一次流行与地域传统的跨界尝试，但音乐层面并未超出常规流行制作范畴，实验性有限，主要价值在于文化表达与议题讨论。

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items._cn_summary: 芬兰手风琴家Maria Kalaniemi与钢琴家Timo Alakotila合作三十五年的专辑，以二重奏为主，偶尔加入弦乐四重奏与无词人声。音乐气质宁静流畅，旋律优美，强调两位乐手之间的默契与即兴对话。曲目包含传统民歌、原创作品以及一首皮亚佐拉与一首芬兰探戈，整体偏向室内乐化的北欧民谣，编曲精致但缺乏实验性与突破性，属于细腻耐听的类型作品。

items._genre: free improvisation / avant-garde jazz / world fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Black Truffle厂牌发行，汇集了Oren Ambarchi、Johan Berthling与Andreas Werliin三位瑞典即兴音乐人，并邀请单簧管演奏家Christer Bothén作为第四位参与者加入。后三者此前以Ghosted三重奏名义已合作完成三张专辑，本次新作延续了此前的即兴框架，但融入了Bothén的单簧管演奏作为新元素，使整体声音更具开放性与探索空间。Bothén的瑞典背景与民族音乐底蕴为这张作品增添了独特的文化维度，与三位音乐人既有的吉他、贝斯与鼓的即兴脉络形成对话。整张专辑呈现出低调而克制的合作美学，强调演奏者之间的倾听与呼应而非主导与独奏，是当代欧洲即兴场景中值得关注的声音。

items.body: Review by Nickmannion — There is a relevance in my intro here...as back in the day in Manchester there used to be a record warehouse called initially Yanks, then Power Cut. I discovered it in the late 70s and it was there till the mid to late 90s. Their main source of stock, which I assume they bought by the pallet load for cents per ten, were cut outs and returns from the States. And they used to knock it out at 99p/�1.29/�1.49/�1.99 an album so you could go in with your �20 (I know, I know...) and come home with 12 albums. It was still the best way to discover new bands or fill gaps in your (at that period my fledgling) collection...Come Taste The Band by Deep Purple for instance (I played it last night, the US release copy I bought there) being my spring to mind example. Yes you may have come home with a couple of clunkers but it also massively broadened your horizons....a Mahavishnu Orchestra release and a Return To Forever album blowing my tiny mind and turning me on to jazz/rock/fusion which I may never have gone near in a million years. So yup, the Pentwater album* looked interesting enough and was �1.29 very well spent 45 years ago. I confess it took a little getting to know as I guess a Montrose/Aerosmith vibe might have been the instant appeal I wanted back then but it was worth hanging on to. Then, and even now, I would have called it 'Art Rock' especially as the intro track Frustration Mass struck me as Zappa (yup about 10 albums over the years from Power Cut!) in a really bad mood or maybe Henry Cow after supplements had worn off. Intriguing if not headbanging....unless you count 'against the wall'. I can now retro fit my expanded knowledge and say a dirtier version of Happy The Man too. There's even a psych type bridge section that adds interest and shows a breadth of influences. Track 2 (Living Room Displays) has a more recognisable keyboard led 'prog' groove that , again with retro knowledge, suggests several bands and a pinch of Kraut maybe. Memo is a more familiar guitar arpeggio song, if not quite mainstream rock then at least less left field. Orphan Girl begins with a Crimson melancholia before several prog bases are firmly touched but in a 'natural' rather than forced construct. AM has strong overtones of say the first two Be Bop Deluxe albums, Palendrobe suggests a Gentle Genesis 'mash up' and War opens with very Atomic Rooster sounding keys with a generous layer of Quatermass sprinkled over. Gwens Madrigal is closer to Kansas do hard rock.I always qualify my use of comparisons being not meant to suggest a very derivative dogs breakfast but as a reference point for new to the band readers and hopefully listeners. Am the first to stick the boot in to slavish copyist bands (hello there Druid and Starcastle....yes....you) but Pentwater, especially from the time and place they came from, did absorb 'unfashionable' influences and turned them into something interesting and unexpected in parts. I now have the follow up album but don't rate it quite as high as the debut. The usual caveat, a 3.8+ rounded up to a 4. Enjoy. * My copy has the same track listing but in a different order to that listed here and, on a quick check, on Discogs too.
items._genre: eclectic prog / art rock / jazz-rock fusion
items._cn_summary: 这张1977年的PENTWATER同名专辑被乐评人描述为融合多种影响的折衷前卫摇滚作品。开篇曲《Frustration Mass》被比作愤怒状态下的Zappa或精神衰退后的Henry Cow，兼具Happy the Man的粗粝质感。《Living Room Displays》呈现键盘主导的前卫律动，带有Krautrock痕迹；《Orphan Girl》以King Crimson式的忧郁开场，却在自然构建中铺展多个前卫元素；《AM》让人联想到Be Bop Deluxe前两张专辑，《Palendrobe》则呈现Gentle Genesis式的拼贴，《War》以Atomic Rooster风键盘开场并融入Quatermass元素，尾曲《Gwens Madrigal》接近硬摇滚化的Kansas。乐评强调这不是简单的模仿拼凑，而是将多种'不合时宜'的影响转化为有趣且出人意料的创作。专辑以小厂牌发行，评论篇幅充实且具个人叙事色彩。

items._cn_summary: 这张1971年的专辑在早期前卫摇滚领域具有探索意义，融合了交响乐编制与即兴器乐段落，音乐盒段落与吉他音色的搭配在当时颇具开创性。Peter Gabriel的演唱方式充满戏剧性与个人色彩，乐评人指出专辑整体有粗糙之处，但某些段落的创意令人难忘。乐评人强调这张作品需要多次聆听才能体会其深层价值，其'笨拙感'反而构成了独特的个人化表达。该评论肯定了乐队在创作路径上的独特性，认为这种不拘常规的手法值得更多乐队效仿。专辑的实验性元素集中在舞台化的呈现和器乐编排的奇异性上，但整体仍属于传统前卫摇滚的范畴。

items.body: Though the author’s scope ranges from the early 19th century to the present day, it is not a comprehensive history, rather it is a sort of micro history of a musical genre born of sadness, hate, anger, and political dominance. It is a genre I have chosen to call “classical protest music”. And, for the sake of this review, I am referring to the incorporation of protest as a valid and effective modality for the contemporary composer.of so called “western art music”, Until the very late 19th century, music served mostly entertainment, celebration, worship, and memorial functions. But this is about a new, if frequently discomforting voice for this art form. Music, like drama, and sometimes poetry are art forms that burn most brightly in performance. They exist on a page or even simply within the artist’s mind but come fully alive only in the temporal realm of performance. They then come to exist in the memories of the individuals who experience it. And those memories also exist concurrently within the overall social reality. Politics, philosophy, economics, and spirituality which ultimately frame art are now incorporated into the art form as it talks back to history. The function of protest music in the popular or vernacular genre, one that arguably has had a greater impact in fomenting political change than than protest music in the guise of the western classical tradition, has been well documented. Not so with music of the concert hall classical format. Jeremy Eichler’s beautifully researched and written micro history makes a case for this art form framing (or reframing) history. Of course, not all expressions of protest hit the target of actually influencing history, but this book is not about that. It is about the birth of a concept little known in music until the late 19th and early 20th century. It is a genre which persists today in the so called political classical genre. The book is filled with historical facts and people which become metaphors as the author elucidates the historical contexts that, in retrospect, can be seen as the genesis of art not just passively responding to historical events. They are attempts to use art to comment about and, hopefully influence history and to express outrage, sadness, and to call for change. Music, ever the realm of entertainment and celebration, now increasingly finds purpose and mechanism to participate, not only as a supplier of entertainment and homage, but also as “a voice crying in the wilderness” in dialogue with the social/political milieu. Eichler chooses four musical pieces by four different composers from four different time periods to tell the story of the evolution of western art music to speak with in an informed, publicly intellectual voice. In its ideal presentation, it succeeds best when it resonates with the hearts and minds of the audience. That can and sometimes does “go viral” (in common parlance) and subsequently influences public opinion. The musical exemplars the author chooses includes: Richard Strauss (1864-1949) “Metamorphosen” (1946) Arnold Schoenberg (1874-1951) “A Survivor from Warsaw” (1947) Benjamin Britten (1913-1976) “War Requiem”(1962) Dimitri Shostakovich (1906-1975) “Symphony No. 13 ‘Babi Yar’” (1962) Each composer, each work is subjected to historical, philosophical, and (I would say) spiritual/mystical analysis. And, to accomplish this, he goes back first to the early 19th century to discuss the rise of the idealized German gconcept of “Bildung” and the subsequent rise of antisemitism famously touted as a necessary fact by Richard Wagner (1813-1883) and subsequently amplified to the extreme of The Shoah. Many musical works are referenced here, but John Foulds “A World Requiem” (1923), which is a large grandiose work of post romantic grandeur that seems to embody many of the elements that have come to characterize classical protest music. The work, written for large forces incorporates both liturgical and non-liturgical texts from disparate sources (not just western literature). It was conceived seemingly as a sort of final statement, a “requiem to end all requiems”, so to speak. Though popular in its day, it no more succeeded in preventing violence and hatred than Alexander Scriabin (1872-1915) in his unfinished Mysterium” succeeded in making the composer an immortal in a transcendent realm described from the spiritual imagination of Theosophical writings. But it did make a huge impact on protest as a valid modality for the artist. Protest in any modality doesn’t always have the intended impact. The point is the statement itself. Foulds’ work can be seen as a sort of precursor, if not template for Britten’s “War Requiem”. More importantly the success of Foulds’work revealed a sympathetic audience who doubtless saw in it a clarion call, a grandly hopeful expression to an audience hungry to resolve the hatred, anger, and sadness of the increasingly divided and chaotic world as it evolved post 1919. It spoke to a fervent hope for healing and transcendence and remains a historically significant work of musical art. Doubtless, many composers were delighted to identify this burgeoning need. Countless works followed Foulds’ noble effort and continue to this day in larger and smaller forces. Protest music, visual art, poetry, and drama are born of pain, sorrow, and hope derived from a sometimes pleading, sometimes shouting optimism. Much like audience engagement in sing alongs, audiences are invited to participate politically, emotionally and share the pain, sadness, and outrage as art speaks back to society rather than simply decorating it or celebrating it. Now, art embraces critique, not simply memorial. Eichler discusses each composer and work, contextualizing them historically, geographically, emotionally, and philosophically/spiritually. Richard Strauss He begins then, with Richard Strauss (1864-1949) and the only work cited here that does not have a vocal component or a text. It is also more a personal reaction rather than an a work explicitly engaging with politics and history. It remains the most unique and enigmatic piece in the oeuvre of a man who remained, if not always happily, employed from the late nineteenth century, through two world wars and horrific historical events and wildly differing leaders. To this listener’s ears, it seems more of a catharsis, a musical processing of the composer’s emotions and possibly exorcizing them and containing them in this music. It is truly a powerful piece but it does not rise to the more explicit protest works that would follow in the mid twentieth century. Arnold Schoenberg A very convincing and insightful analysis is made of the next exemplar of the genre. Eichler’s biographical, historical, and philosophical/spiritual contextualizing of “A Survivor from Warsaw” (1947) seems an unusual choice. But, the fact that this brief monodrama is probably the first major public utterance of the rising awareness of the atrocities described by the narrator and focused attention in a way that only art can. It was also the development of the composer’s revolutionary serially organized music which was, perhaps ironically, very well suited to express the horrors of this age of “great wars”. This section of the book is a masterful integration of political, historical, spiritual elements that provide a compelling mini history, linking individuals and events that shed a fascinating (and devastating) light on this era in musical history. It also places the composer most definitely as a protester, a would be agent of progressive political change. It led this listener to seek to experience more of Schoenberg’s music and was gratified to hear it forever differently and, more so than ever, more essential within western art music. The work was a resounding success at its world premiere in, of all places, New Mexico. The Albuquerque Civic Symphony conducted by Kurt Frederick. 1600 people crowded into the Carlisle Gymnasium on November 4, 1948 were so pleased that the work was repeated, in full, to a deeply moved audience. Hearing this music now, available in many fine interpretations on CD and in video formats, it is all the more stunning that this hardly easy listening tale about horrific events played so well and hit so deeply. And I will never again think of this as one of the composer’s lesser works. Benjamin Britten Moving on to Benjamin Britten and his 1962 “War Requiem”. This music has a prominent place for this writer, having heard a performance by the Chicago Symphony conducted by Mstislav Rostropovich. The cellist, turned conductor was a lifelong progressive political advocate who facilitated a meeting which would become a friendship between Britten and Dmitri Shostakovich among his accomplishments. But, I digress. Eichler’s framing of this composer and music shows a true pacifist composer who encountered the horrors of the First World War as well as subsequent atrocities perhaps one step removed geographically and culturally from the experience of Strauss and Schoenberg. He was a student, then a composer/pianist much admired and supported by the British as he steadily earned his place on the world stage. Early in his rising successes, he managed to insinuate himself to play piano in a series of concerts with Yehudi Menuhin, that toured through war torn Europe to great acclaim. And it is here that the composer encountered first hand, the sights, the stories, the emotions that would forever inform and transform him and his music. This experience is likely one of the seeds that led to the 1962 requiem. Britten utilized the form and Latin texts of the “Missa Pro Defunctis” , the Roman Catholic funeral rites. And he adds a chamber group that plays onstage in front of the full orchestra and chorus (I recall seeing a children’s chorus singing from the topmost seats in Orchestra Hall). The chamber group supports a tenor and a baritone who sing Britten’s settings from the late soldier, then poet/activist Wilfred Owen’s vividly sad and angry poetry. This is a guise not unlike what Leonard Bernstein would do in his anti war “Mass” some 12 years later. Notably, the premiere was to have included tenor Peter Pears (Britten’s life and musical partner), baritone Dietrich Fischer-Dieskau, and soprano Galina Vishnevskaya (later the wife of Mstislav Rostropovich). However the Soviet government prevented her from performing this politically hot work. The hope of symbolically including British, German, and Russian artists was to further emphasize the message of the work. Though Vishnevskaya did participate in the glorious 1963 DECCA recording, she was replaced (most successfully) by the fine British soprano Heather Harper for the premiere. Britten himself conducted the chamber group at the premiere with Meredith Davies leading the large orchestra, choir and soloists. The roofless remains of the original Coventry Cathedral In discussing the War Requiem, Eichler recounts his pilgrimage to the site of the newly rebuilt Coventry Cathedral which had been very badly damaged in the war and the work was commissioned to celebrate the consecration of the new edifice which was built next to the 14th century ruins, ruins through which the audience passed following the very successful premiere on July 27th, 1962. Eichler reports that his own experience walking through the ruins was a powerful experience even now, but especially when one knows this history. Dmitri Shostakovich For the book’s finale, Eichler chose a too little known Shostakovich Symphony, his 13th (1962) ( later titled “Babi Yar”). The composer had worked under the repression of the Soviet Empire at least since his opera “Lady Macbeth of the Mtsensk District” disturbed the Soviet leadership in the 1930s. But he managed to get in a few significant political punches during his long career and continued to produce substantial and fresh new music until his death in 1975. His 5th Symphony won him favor again with the Soviets and the composer’s 7th Symphony “Leningrad”, a paean to the ultimate victory over Nazi forces in 1944 is the stuff of legend, being performed on March 29th of 1942, literally during the siege of Leningrad. Musician soldiers were relieved of their war duties in order to have enough musicians to perform it and strategic bombing raids were done to redirect Nazi bombings and ensure that the music would be heard at its embattled premiere. Eichler’s choice of the 13th Symphony is an apt choice to fit the author’s thesis. The work is a cri de couer, an angry lament raising the awareness of a genocidal slaughter, the evidence of which survived multiple efforts to erase the facts and the evidence from history. It sets the words of the fine Russian poet Yevgeny Yevtushenko (1932-2017) in his poem “Babi Yar” that provided the words. It refers, of course to the genocidal mass murders of Jews, dissidents, and others deemed not worthy of being allowed to live in the Nazi regime at the ravine so named. Accounts vary and much had been done to cover up the murders which numbered up to 30, 000 a day. In fact, there did not exist a memorial for some 100, 000 killed at Babi Yar until 1992. The 13th Symphony premiered on December 18, 1962 in the Great Hall of the Moscow Conservatory. Kiril Kondrashin conducted. Despite controversy and attempts to tamper with the words, pressure to stop the premiere, it was a rousing success. This was only some seven months after the premiere of the Britten War Requiem. Eichler’s account could have ended here but for the fact that, in addition to facilitating a meeting between Britten and Shostakovich, Mistislav Rostropovich smuggled a copy of the 1963 DECCA recording of the War Requiem and a score so that Shostakovich could hear it. And listen he did, with enthusiasm such that Shostakovich was inspired to respond in what would become the composer’s 14th Symphony which was dedicated to Britten. Hence the arts had a conversation about the atrocities of war like never before. The work, incorporating poems by various poets on the subject of death was premiered officially on September 29th, 1969 in Leningrad by the Moscow Chamber Orchestra conducted by Rudolph Barshai. It appears to be inspired in part by the composer’s 1962 orchestration of Modest Mussorgsky’s song cycle, “Songs and Dances of Death” (ca. 1875) and perhaps Gustav Mahler’s “Kindertotenlieder” (1904). The response at the premiere, hardly devoid of criticism, was another resounding success for the aging, ailing composer. The UK premiere was conducted at Aldeburgh by its dedicatee, Benjamin Britten, also to great acclaim. Eichler’s book elegantly describes the genesis of these five works inspired by the history of very real and very shameful atrocities of some 50 years of conflicts which, though they may never be resolved, are truly “Time’s Echo” encased in artistic amber as it were. The memory of this reviewer’s experience of witnessing Maestro Rostrpovich’s reading of Britten’s Requiem so many years later and indeed all subsequent performances of the music chosen here by Eichler hold out a glimmer of hope that these echoes of their time will preserve both the memories of the atrocities themselves as well as the just outrage of the artist’s products in sound for posterity.
items._genre: contemporary classical / protest music / political composition
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非音乐专辑评论，而是对Jeremy Eichler所著《Time's Echo》一书的乐评。该书以微观历史视角，追溯19世纪末以来西方艺术音乐中'抗议'主题的诞生与演变。作者选取四位不同时代作曲家的四部作品，阐述古典音乐如何从服务于娱乐、崇拜与纪念的功能，转向以'声音呼唤于荒野'的姿态介入社会政治语境。文章深入探讨了音乐与历史、政治、哲学之间的对话关系，指出这些作品不仅被动回应历史事件，更试图通过艺术影响历史进程、表达愤怒与悲痛并呼唤变革。全书以丰富史料为支撑，将这些音乐作品视为历史的隐喻，呈现西方古典音乐作为公共知识分子声音的演变轨迹。

items.body: Caught in your head Feel it again What you need now Hope often starts out as a shift in perspective before transforming into something as steady as the stars in the night sky. A person lifts their gaze, allows beauty to feel credible once more, and perceives the future as regaining some of its richness. Music can support this process by creating space for personal experience, presenting an image whose significance shifts depending on who observes it. In this way, light signifies the moment when the world reopens to interpretation, bearing the past while broadening possibilities ahead. That openness runs through “Diamond Rain,” the new single from Los Angeles dark dream-pop duo Magic Wands. Released on August 14th through Metropolis Records, the song finds vocalists and guitarists Dexy and Chris Valentine considering what might appear once a difficult passage in time finally begins to loosen its hold. “The song doesn’t have one fixed meaning. To us, it’s about moving toward the light, finding beauty after darkness and allowing people to discover their own meaning within it.” “Diamond Rain” glows with starfire, carried by a deep, chorus-laden bassline with the imposing scale of 4AD’s post-punk catalog. A crisp drum-machine snare gives the song its dance-floor pull, while sustained guitar hangs overhead in sheets of cold light, breaking into bright points around Dexy’s gauzed lead vocal. The arrangement is dense without becoming airless, and each return to the title phrase seems to lift the music another degree. It ranks among Magic Wands’ most immediate and accomplished songs; six albums into their career, the Valentines plainly still have more than a few tricks up their sleeves. The lyrics start within the mind, where emotions cycle and longing is hard to specify, then shift outward with images of the sun, pale water, lost letters, and departure. “Save it all, for the diamond rain,” Dexy sings. The title presents a compelling contradiction by linking the fury of a storm with the beauty and refraction of a jewel. Its rain can harm, cleanse, hide, or shine light, and the recurring refrain offers a surface for listeners to project their own memories. Magic Wands make that ambiguity visible in the accompanying homemade video “using old cameras, lights and mirrors to create textures and effects that give it a dreamlike feeling.” Extreme close-ups of eyes and mouths overlap with guitars, hands, and ghosted profiles; monochrome images suddenly bloom into acid green, electric blue, and molten red. Bright flecks scatter across the frame like snow caught in headlights as mirrored exposures divide faces into doubles. Elsewhere, horizontal interference and bold blocks of lyric text fill the screen, becoming part of the moving collage. The practical imperfections give the clip its tactile charge, as though vision were returning in fragments of glare, color, and reflection. Watch the video for “Diamond Rain” below: Magic Wands formed in Nashville in 2008 after Chris Valentine discovered Dexy’s song “Teenage Love” online. While they were still living on opposite sides of the country, Chris sent Dexy an actual magic wand through the mail; the gift eventually gave the duo their name. Dexy relocated from Los Angeles to Nashville, and their exchange of songs developed into the Magic Love & Dreams EP in 2009. The xx subsequently remixed their track “Warrior,” while the 2012 debut album Aloha Moon brought the pair to a wider audience and preceded a tour supporting The Jesus and Mary Chain. After settling in Los Angeles, Magic Wands continued with Jupiter (2016), Abrakadabra (2018), Illuminate (2020), Switch (2023), and Cascades (2025). Across those records, Dexy and Chris have shifted between live rhythm sections, drum machines, distorted guitars, and droning synthesizers while retaining the intimate vocal interplay at the center of the band. Their 2026 output has already included the Wishing Well and Remixes EPs, along with their reworking of Peter Murphy’s “Swoon.” “Diamond Rain” now opens the way to a still-untitled Magic Wands album expected in early 2027. “Diamond Rain” is out now via Metropolis Records. Listen to the single on streaming platforms here, and order it here. items.body: Ironic Sweden, the Swedish synthpop and darkwave duo built around producer Dan Ritzen, release “Walk With Angels” on 21 August 2026 through the Danish label Town And Towers Records. The single comes with two remixes and an official video, which premieres on the label’s YouTube channel at midnight Swedish time the same day. It is a song about dying, written in the first person, and Ritzen says he wrote it as an account of how he expects to meet that moment. Ritzen puts the subject plainly rather than at a distance: “A song from the heart. About a subject we rarely talk about. Our own death. I wanted to create a song, where I could explain how I think, I will react on that day. When it’s time for me to go. And tell the people that I’ve done all I wanted to do in my life, so now I can go in peace.” Inside the lyrics of ‘Walk With Angels’ The track sets a hypnotic electronic pulse under melancholic melodies, and the words work through a set of borrowed death images: a dealer handing over a dead man’s hand, coins put aside for the ferryman, a compass needle that no longer points north. The chorus – “Walk with angels / They’ll guide me tonight / I’m leaving earth now without a strife” – reads as acceptance rather than protest. The angels themselves turn out to be less consoling than the chorus suggests. In the final verse they arrive with broken wings and flaming swords, crying, pointing at the narrator. The single is a pre-save at the moment and lands on Spotify, Apple Music, Deezer, Amazon Music, SoundCloud and Tidal on the 21st. It is not on Bandcamp, where Ironic Sweden hosts the rest of its catalogue. The two remixes have been serviced to radio, but neither the remixers nor a separate remix release has been announced. About Ironic Sweden Dan Ritzen started making electronic music in Sweden in the late 1990s as Obscene Inside, working with Fredrik Hansson on an Atari 1040ST and a Yamaha CS1X until Hansson left after about a year. The project became Ironic in the mid-2000s and put out a self-titled EP in a very small run, then took its current name in 2010. The debut EP “Player” followed in December 2017 in an edition of a hundred CDs and records, and remixes of it appeared the following April. Singles and EPs came steadily from there: “King” in October 2018, “Dansmusik” in May 2019, “Pictures” that November, “Dina drömmar” in October 2020, “Universe Friend” in April 2021 and “When I Cry” that October, then the album “Icu” in October 2022. In mid-2023 Ritzen expanded the act into a trio with vocalist Stefan Kauppila Johansson and singer Tezz Markström, and the album “Evolution” arrived on 11 November 2023. Ironic Sweden signed to Town And Towers Records in December 2023, and Side-Line covered the first release under that deal, the double single “Lost Eden” and “Media Whore”, on 22 March 2024. Both sides were produced by Callum Melville, who works as Calibeats; he and his brother Luke later remixed “Media Whore” for a March 2025 release. Markström left in April 2025, and the act has run as a duo since, drawing in guest vocalists on individual tracks – Camila on “My Ego” and Monica on “The Light”, both released on 7 November 2025. “A Night In July” closed 2025 and “Get It Right” followed in February 2026. The band is based in Småland in south-east Sweden and records in a caravan using Logic Pro X, with a sound palette that runs from synthesisers and drum pads through to scrap metal and animal bones. Town And Towers Records, run by Stig Wintendorff out of Gentofte in Denmark, is a member of the Danish independent labels association DUP and works across darkwave, synthpop, italo disco and electropop; Oui Plastique is next on its release schedule, on 4 September. “Walk With Angels” is the first Ironic Sweden single since “Get It Right” in February 2026.
items._cn_summary: Ironic Sweden 是一支瑞典双人组，围绕制作人 Dan Ritzen 建立，作品定位为合成器流行与暗潮的交汇地带。新单曲《Walk With Angels》以催眠式的电子脉冲承载忧郁旋律，歌词以第一人称书写对死亡的态度，借用渡资、死者之手、坏损的罗盘等意象，最终接受而非抗拒这一时刻。副歌呼唤天使同行，但末段揭示天使以破碎之翼与燃烧之剑降临，指向叙述者，带有反讽意味。作品延续了自 1990 年代末以来的电子制作脉络，从 Atari 与 Yamaha CS1X 起步，扩展为当前的三人编制，并在丹麦独立厂牌 Town And Towers Records 发片。整体属于在暗潮与合成器流行传统内的稳定创作，没有展现出对声音设计或结构的显著突破。

items.body: Sina Matix, the Jacksonville dark electro project, released “Killing The Curse” on 7 August 2026 as a standalone digital single. The 4:07 track pushes harder and faster than the surrounding catalogue, setting an angrier vocal against an upbeat EBM pulse. An official video went up on the artist’s own YouTube channel a day earlier, on 6 August. KILLING THE CURSE by SINA MATIX The song is about a stretch of life that does not end on its own. Sina Matix sums it up on the Bandcamp page as “living in toxicity for 5 years and coming to terms that it’s time to reboot your life”, and the press release expands on the same idea: bad luck, divorce, backstabbing and a fear of commitment running for years, until the person finds the strength to press reboot. Where ‘Killing The Curse’ sits in the Sina Matix run of releases The single is self-released and carries no label. It is available as a digital track on Bandcamp in 24-bit/48 kHz, and on Spotify and the other main streaming services. Moon Coil Media handled the announcement. “Killing The Curse” is the fourth Sina Matix release of 2026 and does not belong to “A Dark Place”, the six-track EP issued on 1 May. That run began with the album “Goths Stuck In Airports” on 9 January, followed by the single “This Is Not AI” on 6 March. Two collaborations bookended the turn of the year: “Evil Deals” with Normoria on 2 January and “Crucified” with Matias Nix in December 2025. About Sina Matix Sina Matix is a solo project based in Jacksonville, Florida. The musician behind it does not publish a legal name and works through a chain of aliases: recording as OR from 1995 to 2008, DJing as DJ Question? between 1999 and 2011, then moving into visual work from 2011 as VJ R-M8E and Cinematic Manipulation. The Sina Matix name dates from 2022. Asked directly in a March 2025 interview whether anyone else was involved, the artist answered: “I’m the only one at this point that is part of SINA MATIX.” Side-Line’s earlier coverage notes an origin in Houston, Texas, before the move to Florida. The project’s own label for its music is “dark dramatic electro”, a term it applies to cinematic arrangements built around sampled dialogue and dark subject matter; pushed on genre, the artist points to EBM, darkwave, goth, industrial and film scores, and names Fad Gadget’s “GAG”, Nine Inch Nails’ “The Downward Spiral” and Pink Floyd’s “The Wall” as formative records. The Bandcamp tags on the new single read across the same span, from dark electro and EBM through to industrial techno. The first tracks appeared in 2022 with “Worthless”, followed by “The System” in July 2024 and “Burn” and “Monsters” that September. The debut EP “Cursed” arrived on 31 January 2025 with six tracks on isolation and worthlessness, and Side-Line covered it that February. A signed CD edition limited to fifty numbered copies, “Blessed”, followed on 11 April 2025 with remixes by Assemblage 23, Matt Hart, Ex-VoTo, Stoneburner and Aktivity 512, and the remix album “Burn: The Inferno Mixes” had come out two weeks before that. Singles ran through the rest of 2025: “Flesh and Machine” in September, “Kanokwan” in December and the two collaborations that closed the year. “Killing The Curse” is the sixteenth Sina Matix release on Bandcamp in four years, and the first since “A Dark Place” in May.
items._cn_summary: Sina Matix 来自佛罗里达杰克逊维尔的单人暗潮电子项目，2026年8月发行单曲《Killing The Curse》。作品时长4分07秒，以更猛烈更快的节奏推进，将愤怒人声置于强劲的EBM律动之上。创作动机源于五年有毒生活经历——坏运气、离婚、背刺、承诺恐惧——最终选择按下重启键。文本大量篇幅用于交代发布背景：自发行无厂牌，Bandcamp提供24bit/48kHz音质，Spotify同步上架，Moon Coil Media负责宣发；同时梳理了该项目2025至2026年的完整发行脉络，包括专辑、合作单曲与EP的先后顺序。乐评亦回溯了主理人从1995年至今使用的多个化名与视觉艺术经历，列出Fad Gadget、Nine Inch Nails、Pink Floyd对其影响，并说明其自创术语"暗剧电子"涵盖采样对白、电影化编排与黑暗主题。整体偏向信息梳理型新闻稿而非深度音乐评论。

items.body: Silke Bischoff issued a remastered “Under Your Skin” on 18 August 2026 through Dependent Records. The track first appeared on the German dark wave and synthpop act’s third album “To Protect and to Serve” in 1995 and became the record that carried them onto dance floors beyond the goth scene. It is the second advance single from “Tears – A Collection of Silke Bischoff Songs”, the compilation that opens the band’s reissue campaign, and which production problems have pushed from 4 September to 25 September 2026 in Europe and 2 October in North America. Under Your Skin by Silke Bischoff Axel Kretschmann, who wrote the song with the late Felix Flaucher, connects it to the period the band was in rather than to any single studio decision. “The track ‘Under Your Skin’ was conceived at a time when our collaboration within the band had reached its creative peak”, Kretschmann commented. “While we were working on the album ‘To Protect and to Serve’ it felt as though everything fell naturally into place. Ideas simply popped up, melodies and lyrics fit perfectly, and everything just seemed to happen quite on its own. ‘Under Your Skin’ is one of those songs that reflect this phase best. The track remains at eight minutes but to me it never felt necessary to shorten it. I have always maintained that a song should be exactly as long as it demands – and I would never cut it short just to fit it into an arbitrary radio format.” What is on the Silke Bischoff ‘Tears’ compilation The fourteen-track selection runs “Tears”, “I Don’t Love You Anymore”, “Under Your Skin”, “No Paradise”, “Northern Lights”, “The Union”, “The Man on the Wooden Cross”, “The Letter”, “On the Other Side”, “AJ:NA”, “Benetton Girl”, “Waste of Time”, “Sometimes” and “To Protect and to Serve”. Olaf Wollschläger, whose credits include MESH, Yello, Milú, Melotron and Beborn Beton, remastered the material at Cottonbeat Studio in Burscheid. The opening track is the reason the compilation carries the title it does: “Tears” is a previously unreleased song pulled from the archives, with Flaucher’s vocals on it. It was released with a video in July 2026, directed and filmed by Ronny Zeisberg for wieglas Photo & Film Factory, with the lyrics by Flaucher and the music credited to Kretschmann and Flaucher. The physical edition is a hardcover 48-page CD artbook with photography by Flaucher and liner notes by the German author Mark Urban. It can be pre-ordered from the SPKR store and from Bandcamp. Kretschmann recorded and mixed the source material at Kinderzimmer Studio in Berlin; the artwork is Flaucher’s, laid out by Flaucher, Nico J. and Kretschmann. Silke Bischoff live dates 2026 Three German club shows are booked for release week, with The Second Sight supporting: 25 September 2026 – Bochum, Germany – Matrix 26 September 2026 – Leipzig, Germany – Täubchenthal 27 September 2026 – Berlin, Germany – Columbia Theater About Silke Bischoff Axel Kretschmann and Felix Flaucher founded Silke Bischoff in Germany in 1990 as a gothic and dark wave project, Kretschmann on keyboards, guitar and vocals, Flaucher on vocals. Three two-track demo tapes preceded the self-titled debut, which Chaos issued on vinyl in 1991 and on CD the following year; the underground club track “I Don’t Love You Anymore” came from that period, and “On the Other Side (I’ll See You Again)” became one of the songs most closely associated with the European goth movement. The band name drew immediate objections in Germany. It was taken from the 18-year-old hostage who died in the 1988 Gladbeck hostage crisis, an incident in which the conduct of the press and the police came under heavy public criticism. The founders described the choice as a memorial, on the grounds that the names remembered from such cases are usually the perpetrators’. Guitarist Frank Schwer joined for the second album “The Man on the Wooden Cross”, released by I.N.R.I. Records on 25 October 1993. “To Protect and to Serve” followed on the same label in 1995 and produced “Under Your Skin”. “Northern Lights” arrived in 1996 on I.N.R.I., and the band’s television profile at the time extended to an accusation of promoting Satanism on German TV. Kretschmann left after that run; Flaucher and Schwer continued from 2002 as 18 Summers following a dispute over the name. The three reconciled in 2017 for a private performance among close friends. Flaucher died that August at the age of 59 after a long illness. Kretschmann brought the band back on 8 June 2025 at Wave-Gotik-Treffen in the Agra hall in Leipzig, with guest vocals from Deine Lakaien singer Alexander Veljanov and from Sven Friedrich of Solar Fake, Dreadful Shadows and Zeraphine. The live line-up now pairs Kretschmann with Markus Köster on drums and Andy Simanowitz on piano, keyboards and backing vocals. The band signed to Dependent Records for the catalogue reissues in May 2026, and “Tears” is the first release under that agreement.
items._cn_summary: Silke Bischoff 是德国暗潮与合成器流行代表乐队，新版合辑《Tears》收录14首作品，涵盖1995年专辑《To Protect and to Serve》中的经典曲目《Under Your Skin》以及此前未发表的《Tears》。文章主要报道了2026年8月发行的重制单曲、9月合辑的发售延期情况以及实体版本的设计——一本48页精装CD艺术册，收录Felix Flaucher的摄影作品及德国作家Mark Urban撰写的文案。Olaf Wollschläger在Cottonbeat Studio完成母带重制，原始录音由Kretschmann在柏林Kinderzimmer Studio完成。这篇文章属于唱片发行的资讯新闻，缺乏对音乐本体、编曲特征或艺术成就的深入评析，更接近厂牌宣传稿的转载内容。

items.body:
Moving sideways from Warp to Domino, Simian Mobile Disco's James Ellis Ford challenges himself on his second solo full-length, crafting a set of Sakamoto-inspired synth pop from his hospital bed.

Ford's always been capable of producing pitch-perfect pop - his appearance on records from everyone from the Pet Shop Boys to Depeche Mode is a testament to that - but 'Lost in Another World' is a more personal affair. It was written and produced in hospital after he'd been diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia last year, "on the ward between rounds of chemo." Thankfully his condition has improved - he posted earlier this month that he's got no more treatment in store - but the album stands as a vulnerable reflection of a difficult time. Ford describes it as a "pep talk", and it draws on some of his most enduring influences, Yellow Magic Orchestra and Japan, to channel its complicated tangle of emotions. 

On the opening track (and lead single) 'Overtones', Ford's voice hovers over plasticky rhythmelodic sequences and rubbery '80s drums and you'd be forgiven for assuming it's a lost city pop demo. Ford doesn't let the energy fall off, either, waltzing through slow-motion melancholia on the tentatively beautiful 'Here Today' and John Foxx-style synth pop on 'This Too Shall Pass'. Ultimately, it's surprisingly hopeful material, infused with genuine feeling.
items._cn_summary: James Ellis Ford 在急性髓系白血病治疗期间于医院完成第二张个人专辑，从 Warp 转投 Domino。他称这张作品是给自己的“打气话”，以坂本龙一、Yellow Magic Orchestra 与 Japan 为底色，将化疗期间的脆弱情绪转化为略带塑料质感的节奏序列、弹性 80 年代鼓机与慢速忧郁旋律。开篇曲听感近似失落城市流行样本，随后在《Here Today》的迟缓伤感与《This Too Shall Pass》的 John Foxx 式合成器流行中保持情绪张力；整体并未沉溺于阴郁，而是透出真诚的希望感。

I entered some of the phrases from the music on the strange A-side in websearch and out popped the A-side from the LP "The Groundhogs - Who Will Save The World? The Mighty Groundhogs" by the Groundhogs.So the root cause is a mixup by the recording company when the album was pressed. items.excerpt: Rosetta Stone, the gothic rock project Porl King has fronted since 1988, release “Executing Nostalgia” on 25 September 2026 through Cleopatra Records. The first single, “Shadowban”, arrived on 18 August with an official video on the label’s channel and runs 3:41. items.body: Rosetta Stone, the gothic rock project Porl King has fronted since 1988, release “Executing Nostalgia” on 25 September 2026 through Cleopatra Records. The first single, “Shadowban”, arrived on 18 August with an official video on the label’s channel and runs 3:41. Cleopatra’s Dave Thompson describes it as “the driving, near-Motorik pulse” of the record, “a mantric chant that could go easily have lasted far longer than its 3 minute 40 lifespan”. What is on Rosetta Stone’s ‘Executing Nostalgia’ The album runs ten tracks: “Shadowban”, “Someone”, “Regression”, “Negative”, “Rejection”, “Incubus Succubus”, “Pagan Love Song”, “Alone”, “Moya” and “Talk About The Weather”. Four of those titles reach back into the early-1980s post-punk and positive-punk records King grew up on. “Moya” was Southern Death Cult’s debut single in December 1982; “Pagan Lovesong” came out on Rough Trade in June 1982 for the Virgin Prunes; “Talk About The Weather” is the title track of Red Lorry Yellow Lorry‘s 1985 debut on Red Rhino. Bandcamp credits “Incubus Succubus” as a feature with Thunder Bae, whom Cleopatra describes as “a rising star in the German electronic scene”. That makes “Executing Nostalgia” a second record in eighteen months built partly on other people’s songs, after the all-covers collection “Nothing Is Sacred” in February 2025. Executing Nostalgia by Rosetta Stone Cleopatra Records has the album on CD, cassette and a black, gold and white splatter vinyl LP, with a signed test pressing offered separately. All formats are open for pre-order through the label’s own store, and the digital edition is on Bandcamp. About Rosetta Stone Porl King and bassist Karl North formed Rosetta Stone in Liverpool in 1988, filling out the line-up with a drum machine and synth rack they called Madame Razor. Early tape-only releases through 1988 and 1989 and support slots with The Mission built the audience for the debut album “An Eye for the Main Chance” in 1991, by which point Porl Young had joined as second guitarist. The 12-inch “Adrenaline” followed as their widest-reaching single, and a cover of The Rattles’ “The Witch” appeared in 1992. Cleopatra Records signed the band in the United States and issued “Foundation Stones” and the “Adrenaline” compilation in 1993. “The Tyranny of Inaction” arrived in 1995, recorded after the advance paid for an Alesis ADAT and pushed the guitars into a harder electronic setting; “Hiding in Waiting” followed in 1996. King lost part of his left little finger in an accident late in 1997, which changed how he played. The band split in 1998 after “Chemical Emissions” and a limited remix disc, closing with a headline set at Whitby Gothic Weekend that October; North joined Dream Disciples. A contractual album of New Romantic covers, “Unerotica”, closed the first run in 2000. King spent the following years on Miserylab and then In Death It Ends, and produced and remixed for other artists. He restarted Rosetta Stone as a solo concern in 2019 with “Seems Like Forever”, mixed by Jürgen Engler of Die Krupps, and has kept a steady pace since: “Cryptology” in August 2020, “Under The Weather” on 30 August 2024, “Nothing Is Sacred” on 14 February 2025 and “Dose Makes The Poison” on 20 August 2025. Cleopatra has run a parallel reissue programme across the same period, including the “Anthology 1988-2012” box set. “Executing Nostalgia” is the fourth Rosetta Stone album in just over two years, and follows “Dose Makes The Poison” by thirteen months.
items._cn_summary: 这是一篇关于Rosetta Stone新专辑《Executing Nostalgia》的纯新闻稿，介绍了发行信息、曲目列表及乐队历史。文章提到首支单曲《Shadowban》被描述为'近Motorik的律动脉冲'，专辑中有四首曲目翻自1980年代初的后朋克作品，包括Southern Death Cult、Virgin Prunes和Red Lorry Yellow Lorry的旧作，并与德国电子音乐人Thunder Bae合作了一首。文章重点在厂牌发行格式和乐队组建背景，对音乐本身的分析极为有限。作为一支1988年成立的哥特摇滚乐队，Rosetta Stone的创作以翻唱他人作品为主，风格延续传统的后朋克与暗潮路线，未见明显的实验性突破或跨类型融合。原文信息密度不足且属于新闻通稿性质，缺乏深入的乐评视角。

items.body: Phoenix post-punk and darkwave artist Alex Okami released “Permanent Disease” as a digital single on July 30, 2026, and the track now opens a seven-date US run booked across California, Arizona, Colorado, New Mexico, Texas and Nevada in September 2026. Okami wrote and performed the song. Manuel Perez produced, mixed and mastered it, and added synths. Okami has tied the lyric directly to his own health rather than to a character or a scenario. It’s a song about life-long ailments taking hold of your mental and physical health to the point that it feels like your world is permanently over. As a sufferer of negative health conditions, I needed an outlet to express how I was feeling about my situation. The track runs 2:49 and is the only piece on the release. It is available on Bandcamp and on streaming services, with no physical edition announced. Okami tags it as post-punk, darkwave, goth and indie electronic. Permanent Disease by Alex Okami Alex Okami ‘Permanent Disease’ brings a new production credit The Perez credit is the change here. Okami’s earlier recordings were handled by Caleb DiLoreto, who mixed, mastered and engineered both “The Strange EP” and the “Strange As Angels” album, and who also performed on the 2021 single “The Wolf”. “Permanent Disease” is the first Okami release with Perez in the production, mixing and mastering chair. It is also the third standalone single in nine months, after “Holy Water” on November 20, 2025 and “Night Terrors” on February 10, 2026. No album or EP has been announced to collect them. The three singles also mark a change of release pattern. Everything Okami issued before them was gathered into an EP or an album, and each of those came with a physical run: “The Strange EP” as a cassette, “Strange As Angels” as an ultra clear 12-inch vinyl with black splatter and as a limited clear cassette. Both cassette editions are now sold out. The 2025 and 2026 singles have stayed digital. Tour dates for Alex Okami in September 2026 The run opens in Los Angeles and closes in Las Vegas, with a Phoenix hometown date at a record shop in between. 12.09.2026 – Los Angeles, CA, USA – The Paramount 13.09.2026 – Tempe, AZ, USA – Lighthouse Kava Bar 18.09.2026 – Trinidad, CO, USA – Trinidad Lounge 19.09.2026 – Santa Fe, NM, USA – Hotel Glorieta 20.09.2026 – El Paso, TX, USA – Rosewood Bar 22.09.2026 – Phoenix, AZ, USA – Central Records 26.09.2026 – Las Vegas, NV, USA – The Griffin About Alex Okami Alex Okami is a solo post-punk and darkwave project based in Phoenix, Arizona. The first release under the name was the five-track EP “Under the Same Moon”, issued on April 3, 2020 and made up of “New Me Knew You”, “Bones”, “Veins”, “Severed Silhouette” and “Lunar Fever”. A gap of more than a year followed before the single “The Wolf” on August 1, 2021. Okami wrote it and performed it with Caleb DiLoreto, who mixed, mastered, produced and engineered the recording at Mercy Recordings. DiLoreto stayed on for the next two releases. Physical output began in 2025. “The Strange EP” appeared on January 25, 2025 in a cassette-only edition limited to 20 copies, collecting “In the Dark”, “Vampiros”, “Under My Skin”, “Haunted By You” and “In the Dark (Corbeau Hangs Remix)”. DiLoreto mixed, mastered and engineered it, Nick Toppel added guitar, and Okami supplied the artwork. The debut album “Strange As Angels” followed on March 20, 2025 with nine tracks: “In the Dark”, “Telarañas”, “Under My Skin”, “Monster”, “Vampiros”, “Gloom Culture”, “Blood Bond”, “Haunted By You” and “Twilight”. Four of the five songs from the cassette EP carried over, and the record extended the same set with new material. A remix of “Vampiros” by Male Tears sits alongside it on Okami’s Bandcamp page. Since the album, the project has moved on singles: “Holy Water” in November 2025, “Night Terrors” in February 2026 and now “Permanent Disease”. The September run is the first announced touring block behind them.
items._cn_summary: 这篇文章并非乐评，而是Side-Line发布的新闻稿，介绍了Alex Okami新单曲《Permanent Disease》的发行信息、巡演日程以及制作团队变动。文章提到该曲为2分49秒的数字单曲，由Manuel Perez接手制作、混音和母带工作，取代了此前合作的Caleb DiLoreto。歌曲主题围绕长期疾病对身心健康的影响展开，是创作者个人经历的直接表达。文中还梳理了Okami从2020年首张EP到近期的发行脉络，指出此前作品均有实体版本，而2025至2026年的三支单曲均为数字发行。文章缺乏对音乐本身的深入分析与评论，仅停留在资讯层面。

items.body: The Electrozixx are a synthpop and electropop duo from Floreffe, in the Belgian province of Namur, and their fifth EP, “Frenchy Touch“, came out on 25 June 2026. Six tracks, recorded at Noise Factory Studio in nearby Wierde and mixed and mastered by Peter Rainman of the French act People Theatre, it is the pair’s second release with Rainman at the desk. Singer and lyricist Cat and keyboard player, composer and producer Fred founded the project in late 2023. Their Facebook page dates the start to 27 November 2023. The two mix bright synthesizer lines, mid-tempo electronic rhythms and Cat’s lead vocal, and name Depeche Mode, OMD, Yazoo, Pet Shop Boys and Alphaville as reference points. Their own bio puts the aim as combining “the timeless spirit of classic synthpop with a fresh, contemporary sound”. Frenchy Touch by The Electrozixx “Frenchy Touch” runs “Paris – London”, “Mystery”, “Dreams”, “New Age”, “Echoes of the Past” and “Tu n’en finis pas”, the last of these sung in French. The duo wrote and produced the material themselves and made the artwork and visuals. The Electrozixx have released five EPs since January 2025 The band’s catalogue is short and closely spaced. “Free My Soul” came out on 25 January 2025, “Revelation” on 13 February 2025, “New Frequencies” on 4 June 2025 and “Belgian Synthpower” on 2 November 2025, each running six tracks, with several of the songs having appeared first as standalone singles from October 2024 onward. Rainman mixed and mastered “Belgian Synthpower” as well, and remixed “Endless Conversations” from “New Frequencies” as the standalone “People Theatre’s desire mix”, posted on 21 September 2025. The duo name the UK independent East London Recordings as their label on their Bandcamp and Facebook pages. None of the five EPs carries a label credit on Bandcamp or Discogs, and the releases are distributed digitally. About The Electrozixx The Electrozixx were formed in late 2023 in Floreffe, province of Namur, by Cat, who writes the lyrics and sings, and Fred, who plays keyboards, composes and produces. Neither publishes a surname. The pair issued their first standalone singles, “Free My Soul” and “Fire”, on 19 October 2024, followed by “When I’m with You” on 2 November 2024, “Take a Ride” on 23 November 2024 and “Magic Everywhere” on 21 December 2024. Those tracks were collected on the debut EP “Free My Soul” in January 2025. Three more EPs followed within the year. Peter Rainman, who founded People Theatre in October 1993 and has remixed Nitzer Ebb, IAMX, Anne Clark, Haujobb, Apoptygma Berzerk and Trisomie 21, began working with the duo on “Belgian Synthpower” and returned for “Frenchy Touch”. Recording has stayed at Noise Factory Studio in Wierde, about fifteen kilometres from Floreffe. The five EPs are on Bandcamp and on the main streaming services. The band have not announced live dates.

items.body: Work. Sleep. Rinse. Repeat. The humdrum of modern life can be a burdensome weight that feels unbearable at times. Admittedly, I have recently been struggling with the existential malaise of seemingly endless repetition of routines in both my personal and professional lives. Even the habits that I normally enjoy or that keep me healthy have felt tedious. That’s why it feels serendipitous that Sisyphean Life, the newest collection of grindcore from long-running Dutch quartet Suffering Quota, came up for review. What better way to marinate in those feelings of listlessness than by reviewing an album themed around that very topic?The aptly titled Sisyphean Life explores the “depression and boredom of modern daily life” and its “endless cycles and neverending days” that occur while we “chase fleeting moments of bliss forevermore.” Prevalent throughout the album is a sinking sensation of existential oppression that is carried by the themes and performances. What stands out the most in this respect is Gerald Timmermans’ pained and claustrophobic vocals, which often sound as if he is shrieking for help while being buried alive under the weight of life’s mundane routines and quotidian tasks. Other moments demonstrate a similar notion. The closing 7/8 riff in “Overpowering Weight” is performed in dramatically decreasing tempos, conjuring the image of someone dragging ever-increasing amounts of weight until they are unable to move with any more forward momentum. According to the band, this was an intentional link the band wanted to make between the music and lyrics. Similarly, the trudging, repetitive riff that makes up half of “Slope” elicits images of suit-wearing office workers with dead eyes plodding their way toward grey office buildings. Other noteworthy parts, such as the brief glimpses of mournful melodicism that cut through the aggression on “Dust” and “Strain Once More” end much too soon, but they are moments that shine a light through the oppression.Despite the consistent quality of the Dutch quartet’s creative (but sporadic) output over their 15-year career, suffering Quota have always existed on the periphery of a genre that has itself always been on the periphery. In many ways, that doggedness is a rejection of the resigned monotony represented by the myth of Sisyphus. Sisyphean Life may be primarily concerned with that resigned monotony, but Suffering Quota's resilience and the quality of their output repudiates it. Sisyphean Life by Suffering Quota
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑以碾核为载体，探讨现代日常生活的抑郁与重复感。主唱Gerald Timmermans的嗓音充满痛苦与幽闭感，仿佛在生活重压下呼救。音乐上通过结构设计强化主题，例如《Overpowering Weight》结尾的7/8拍riff以逐渐减速的方式表现负重前行，《Slope》中沉重重复的riff则描绘了面无表情的上班族走向灰色办公楼。专辑中偶尔闪现的哀伤旋律片段短暂却醒目，为压迫感注入一丝光亮。乐队以十五年的坚持和稳定输出，在边缘类型中保持着自身韧性，其创作虽未脱离碾核框架，但在节奏与情绪表达上具有一定巧思。

items._cn_summary: 英国乐队Hard-Fi时隔15年推出的新专辑，延续了以disco、dub和reggae为基底、映射劳动阶层情感与生活的创作路线。作品中既有与哥伦比亚裔说唱者合作、融入cumbia节奏的曲目，也有巴利阿里式慢速电子氛围的中板歌曲，展现出乐队在既有风格之外的自然延伸。整体上，专辑在保持根源性表达的同时，尝试加入更多元的节奏元素，但整体仍属于独立摇滚范畴，与实验性或前卫方向距离较远。

items.body:
Tiny Sun creates tiny songs that give off light and heat well out of proportion to their size. Composed, performed, and produced by Martina Sorbara, Jonathan Goldsmith, and Don Rooke, the record is vaguely Americana, with plucked guitars and ukuleles, chiming keyboards, and the lonesome slide of the guitar.
Vanishment
contains eighteen sparkling miniatures - that take a scant 34 minutes to negotiate - notable for their economy of arrangement and the subtle directness of the lyrics. The tracks glow with Martina�s clear, high, and sometimes fragile voice.
The songs are about loss: lost love, lost confidence, but sometimes about resignation to the enigmatic quirks of the world. The tone of wry fatalism mirrors the fact that this project is the work of many years of collaboration and email exchanges while the trio pursued their musical day jobs. Jonathan Goldsmith is an award-winning composer for television and film, Don Rooke fronts the Toronto roots band The Henrys, and Martina Sorbara is known for folk, electropop, and her band Dragonette.
Kerosene Madrigal
The range of backgrounds leads to many styles, and the record betrays interesting influences. The opening track, �Kerosene Madrigal,� is a sort of miner�s blues reminiscent of Michelle Shocked. The soul-country of �Imagined Love� reminded me of fellow Torontonians Cowboy Junkies, especially the sweet organ. The stoic and twangy �Don�t Fault the Stars for Falling� could have been a Dolly Parton tune.
A Grand Expanse
�A Grand Expanse� has a more ambitious arrangement.  It sounds like the end-credits song from a long-ago film we only vaguely remember. It says everything it needs to in one minute and twenty seconds and exactly 38 words. It is quintessential Tiny Sun.
The entire recording feels like music from a dream, and since no one knows exactly what dream music sounds like, this could be it.
Berceuse
Tiny Sun will perform the entire album at Toronto�s Koerner Hall on May 14, 2026.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由Martina Sorbara、Jonathan Goldsmith和Don Rooke三人组成的Tiny Sun创作，收录了18首短小精悍的歌曲，总时长仅34分钟。编曲以原声吉他、尤克里里、键盘和滑棒吉他为主，呈现简约而直接的质感。歌词围绕失去、宿命与对世界怪诞之处的顺从展开，带有一种冷幽默的宿命论色彩。乐评指出其风格涉猎广泛，从开篇的矿工蓝调、灵魂乡村到类似Dolly Parton的乡村曲调均有体现，整体氛围如同模糊记忆中的梦境配乐。作品源自三人多年的合作与邮件往来，融合了各自在影视配乐、根源摇滚和流行电子领域的背景，但最终呈现为一张典型的当代美式民谣唱片，与实验、前卫或电子音乐路线相距较远。

items.body: Review by ianjferris@gmail.com — I've seen all the reviews here of "Open Your Eyes" and believe me, I do understand why so many are scoring this album with only one or two stars, with some scathing commentary as an accompaniment. However, I can't do scathing for this album. It's too good for that. The musicians on it are much too good for that. I have to award this album four stars. When I look at this album with both my ears and my eyes open (all puns intended), the absence of Rick Wakeman is clearly obvious; but not in a negative way. I hear a very good album of pop songs (albeit with many being a bit on the quirkey side), put together by a collection of very experienced, very talented musicians. This isn't a progressive rock album. I don't believe that it was ever supposed to be a prog album. I think that at this stage, just after the "Keys To Ascension" recordings, the YES guys just might have been "all progged out". After all, they were all human (some still are, allegedly). The result was that all they had left was to put together some simple easy listening pop music pieces. Well, that's what it sounds like to me. The thing is though, said "simple easy listening pop music pieces" were actually being produced by serious prog rock musicians. And as a consequence, there are many musical flourishes evident throughout. And that's why it falls between two stools; two very distinct stools - good pop music and good prog music. There clearly are elements of both pop and prog here in this album. Just not enough to satisfy the purists (whether pop purists or prog purists). But outside of that, there is plenty to satisfy the broader mind. The only issue resides in the final, hidden (so called) track. Even for the most hardened, card carrying, prog adventurists, this one is a bit of a mystery. Mind you though, I can clearly imagine Squire, Anderson et al, smirking and sniggering mischievously at including this one curiosity.Anyway, I like this album enough to award it four stars.PS - I have the album on vinyl. Double album coloured vinyl. LP one is orange. LP two is red, both 180gram vinyl. It's one of 3000 copies that were issued by EAR Music.Just showing off.....
items._genre: pop rock / soft rock / progressive pop
items._cn_summary: 这张1997年专辑被评论者视为Yes乐队在长篇前卫作品之后转向流行音乐的一次尝试。评论者认为乐队成员在经历密集的前卫创作后，选择了制作简单易听的流行歌曲，但这些歌曲仍带有前卫音乐家的精致编排痕迹，因此作品同时具备流行与前卫两种特征，却都无法充分满足各自领域的纯粹爱好者。专辑缺少Rick Wakeman的键盘参与，评论者认为其本质上是经验丰富的前卫乐手创作的轻量级流行作品。整体定位介于流行与前卫之间，以音乐细节和制作精良见长，但在前卫实验性方面较为有限。评论者给予四星评价，认为对广义听众而言仍有足够吸引力。
